- **Hour 2026-06-11 19:03 KST:** read paper 142 — *PhysX-3D: Physical-Grounded 3D Asset Generation* (Ziang Cao, Zhaoxi Chen, Liang Pan, Ziwei Liu — **NTU S-Lab + Shanghai AI Lab**, arXiv:2507.12465 v4 28 Nov 2025, **NeurIPS 2025 Spotlight**). The *3 killer contributions* are **(a) PhysXNet dataset** (26K PartNet objects with *part-level* physics annotations across 5 dimensions: absolute scale + material + affordance + kinematics + descriptions, the *first* 3D dataset with abundant properties for each part, built via GPT-4o VLM + human verification, the *exact* same recipe as Pixie 141's VLM-actor-critic), **(b) PhysXNet-XL dataset** (6M procedurally generated objects, the *killer* scaling trick — sample (E, ν, ρ) from learned PhysXNet distributions + procedurally compose parts + procedurally compose kinematic trees, *zero* human annotation, *zero* LLM calls), and **(c) PhysXGen dual-branch architecture** (2-stage VAE + flow-matching on (z_struct dim 1024 + z_phys dim 8) latents, image-conditioned via frozen DINOv2+CLIP-ViT-L/14 tokenizers, *partial* freezing — structural encoder frozen + structural decoder fine-tuned + physics branch trained from scratch, ~2-second inference on single A100, *3 orders of magnitude faster* than test-time-optimization methods). - **Hour 2026-06-11 18:03 KST:** read paper 141 — *Pixie: Fast and Generalizable Supervised Learning of 3D Physics from Pixels* (Long Le, Ryan Lucas, Chen Wang, Chuhao Chen, Dinesh Jayaraman, Eric Eaton, Lingjie Liu — **UPenn + MIT**, arXiv:2508.17437 v2 26 Aug 2025, **ICLR 2026**). Key insight: **the *direct concurrent competitor* to VoMP (paper 140), the *only two* feed-forward material-field predictors in the 141-paper reading list, with *orthogonal* design choices — VoMP uses *DINOv2* + *voxelized multi-view* + *12-layer Geometry Transformer* (the *geometric* material predictor, best for shape-conditioned material gradient), Pixie uses *CLIP* + *distilled NeRF feature field* + *3D U-Net* (the *semantic* material predictor, best for text-aligned material class), the *killer* design lesson is that *CLIP > RGB and CLIP > occupancy* for material prediction (Table 1: 0.985 vs 0.643-0.722 material class accuracy, 4.35 vs 1.76-2.53 VLM realism), the *direct* empirical evidence that *material is a semantic concept requiring semantic features* — only CLIP has been explicitly trained to associate visual features with semantic labels**. The *3 killer results* are **(a) 1.46-4.39× VLM-realism improvement over DreamPhysics/OmniPhysGS/NeRF2Physics** (with 4.35 VLM vs best-baseline 2.53), **(b) 2-second inference** (vs hours for test-time optimization, **3 orders of magnitude faster**), and **(c) zero-shot sim-to-real transfer** — train on synthetic PixieVerse (1624 Objaverse assets, 10 semantic classes, 5 material types) and *zero-shot* predict materials of real-world NeRF scenes (LERF, Spring-Gaus datasets), the *only* method in the paper that can do this, the *strongest* H5 evidence in the dental-relevant literature. The *3 killer design tricks* are **(1) distilled CLIP NeRF feature field (Shen et al. 2023)** for 2D-to-3D CLIP lifting (the *de facto* 2D-to-3D bridge, the *exact* template for v0 sub-task 4's 2D-image-to-3D-material-field), **(2) explicit occupancy mask** for 98% background sparsity (the *killer* practical detail, *exactly* the same sparsity pattern as dental-crown material fields where most of the volume is air/gum), and **(3) VLM-actor-critic labeling pipeline** with Gemini-2.5-Pro + manually-tuned in-context examples (the *killer* H5 mechanism, Table 2 shows removing in-context examples drops VLM score 3.6× from 4.83 to 1.34, the *single most-expensive and most-valuable* component of the data pipeline, the *direct* precedent for v0's dental-VLM + dental-consultant in-context examples). The *license* is **MIT** ✅ (the *most-permissive* license in the feed-forward-material-field pair, with VoMP Apache 2.0; MIT allows closed-source commercial deployment with NO attribution required, the *killer* v0 v1 commercial-deployment license). The *v0 action* is to **adopt Pixie as the v0 sub-task 4 (occlusion simulation) material-field predictor** ($0 Lambda for the pre-trained weights, $50-100 Lambda for dental fine-tuning, 1-2 weeks engineering; the *killer* practical feature: ~2s per object on a single A100, 10× faster than VoMP's 3.6s, ~$0.20-0.50 per dental arch inference, *fast enough* for clinical chairside use; the *MIT license* means v0 can ship a *closed-source* commercial product with no attribution required). The *v0 v0 v1 action* is to **combine VoMP (DINOv2+Transformer) + Pixie (CLIP+U-Net) for the best-of-both-worlds material field** (concatenate 768-dim DINOv2 + 768-dim CLIP → 64³×1536 input → 3D U-Net → per-voxel material field; $50-100 Lambda for combined-feature training, 1-2 weeks engineering; the *de facto* v0 v1 design that combines the strengths of *both* feed-forward material-field predictors). The *v0 v0 v2 action* is to **adopt Pixie's VLM-actor-critic labeling pipeline as the v0 H5 mechanism** (3DTeethSeg22 + ToSynFCD for part-segmented assets + dental-VLM as VLM actor + dental-critic/human-dentist as VLM critic + 10-20 manually-tuned dental-material in-context examples for enamel/dentin/pulp/cementum/gum/titanium/zirconia/PFM; produces 1K-10K dental arches with spatially-varying (E, ν, ρ) fields; $50 Lambda + $500-1K dental consultant for in-context examples, 2-3 weeks engineering). The *hypothesis impact*: **H1 PARTIAL SUPPORT** (2-stage CLIP-NeRF + U-Net is *exactly* H1's "decompose the problem", but Pixie's 2 stages are "feature-distillation + supervised regression", not "VAE+DDM"), **H2 PARTIAL CONTRADICTION** (Pixie is *deterministic* feed-forward, no diffusion; but the paper *explicitly acknowledges* future work should learn a *distribution* of materials via diffusion, the H2 *extension*), **H3 NOT TESTED** (Pixie conditions on *single object* multi-view RGB, not on *multi-context* like the 6-tooth dental context; the multi-view is *internally* H3 via the CLIP-NeRF feature field), **H4 STRONG CONTRADICTION** (Pixie predicts material on an *explicit* voxel grid (64³, 262K voxels) then transfers to an *explicit* 3DGS for MPM; implicit representations not used; *direct* contradiction to H4 for material prediction, *consistent* with VoMP), **H5 STRONGEST SUPPORT IN 141-PAPER READING LIST (tied with LRM-Zero 111)** (zero-shot sim-to-real transfer is the *killer* Pixie result, the *direct* evidence that *CLIP's pre-training on real images* provides the *sim-to-real* prior that *synthetic-only training* lacks; for v0 v0 v1 v2 (dental), this is the *killer* precedent: train on synthetic Objaverse (or our Zeroverse-dental), zero-shot transfer to real dental scans). **Critical insight for the *hybrid* v0 architecture:** **VoMP (DINOv2+Transformer, Apache 2.0) + Pixie (CLIP+U-Net, MIT) = the *de facto* v0 v1 best-of-both-worlds material-field predictor** for v0 sub-task 4, *combined* with DMC 033 + Hwang 061 histogram loss + DuoDent 059 O_ce+O_cp for the *full* clinical 3D-gen stack. **★ CORRECTION TO 140-VOMP NOTE:** the 140-VoMP note claimed "VoMP is the *first* and *only* feed-forward material-field predictor" — this is *correct* as of paper 140, but paper 141 (Pixie) is the *concurrent* feed-forward material-field predictor, so the *correct* claim is "VoMP and Pixie are the *only two* feed-forward material-field predictors in the 141-paper reading list, with orthogonal design choices (DINOv2+Transformer vs CLIP+U-Net) and orthogonal strengths (geometric vs semantic)". **★ Open question for HK:** for v0 v0 v1 v1 clinical deployment, do we *adopt both* (VoMP+Pixie combined, the *de facto* best-of-both-worlds) or *adopt one* (VoMP for the Apache 2.0 license vs Pixie for the MIT license)? Recommendation: *adopt both* for v0 v0 v1, the *killer* v0 paper differentiator is "first dental-crown paper with combined CLIP+DINOv2 material-field prediction". Note in `papers/141-pixie-le25.md`. **Next paper to read (142):** the 141-Pixie note's recommended next is **(a) PhysX-3D (Cao et al. 2025, arXiv:2507.12465, the *joint shape+material generative model* that uses TRELLIS structural latent + learned material latents, the *direct* complement to VoMP 140 + Pixie 141 for v0 sub-task 1 joint shape+material generation), or (b) SLAT-Phys (arXiv:2603.23973, Mar 2026, the *very recent* structured-latent material-field predictor that *explicitly* compares to Pixie, the *killer* paper for understanding 2026 SOTA), or (c) SOPHY (Cao et al. 2025, the *3D generative model* with simulation-ready outputs and material decoder, the *direct* comparison to Pixie+VoMP for *generative* material prediction). **Recommendation: read 142 = PhysX-3D** — the *most recent* and *most directly relevant* to v0 sub-task 1 (joint shape+material generation), the *missing* modality for our pipeline since VoMP 140 and Pixie 141 are purely *predictive* (input: existing shape, output: material field) and our v0 sub-task 1 needs to *generate* the shape+material jointly.

- **Hour 2026-06-09 10:03 KST:** read paper 087 — *VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer* (Wang, Chen, Karaev, Vedaldi, Rupprecht, Novotny, VGG Oxford + Meta AI, arXiv:2503.11651, 14 Mar 2025, **CVPR 2025 Best Paper Award**). Key insight: **the *categorical* paradigm shift from 6-stage iterative 3D pipelines (COLMAP: 15+ sec, DUSt3R/MASt3R: 7-9 sec, 2-image pairs + global alignment) to a *single 1.2B-param feed-forward transformer* (24 alternating frame-wise/global self-attention blocks, frozen DINOv2-L tokenizer, 1 camera + 4 register tokens per frame, DPT dense decoder) that takes up to hundreds of unposed RGB images and predicts ALL 3D attributes (camera intrinsics+extrinsics, depth maps, point maps, 3D point tracks, per-pixel aleatoric uncertainty) in ONE forward pass in ~0.2 sec for 10 images, *often* outperforming optimization-based baselines *without* any post-processing (AUC@30 on RealEstate10K: VGGT 85.3 / VGGT+BA 93.5 vs DUSt3R 79.2 / MASt3R 81.7 / COLMAP 78.0, the *single largest* jump in the 3D-from-2D literature) — the *direct* H1 evidence that joint multi-task foundation model > per-task specialists, with the *killer* finding that predicting all 3D tasks *jointly* improves *every individual task* (+15% point-map accuracy over depth-only, because the multi-task loss enforces internal geometric consistency as a self-supervision signal, the *asymmetric* task-dependence rule: removing camera drops pointmap 15%, removing depth drops 8%, removing pointmap *improves* the other two, the *practical* design rule for any future multi-task 3D transformer)**. The *3 killer results* are **(a) Feed-forward VGGT beats optimization on all 4 tasks** (camera pose, multi-view depth, dense point cloud, 3D point tracking) on every dataset, **(b) Alternating attention is the *right* inductive bias** (Table 5: alternating 0.709 < global-only self-att 0.85 < cross-att 1.061, the *cleanest* design validation, the field should converge on alternating for any multi-view-to-3D transformer), **(c) Combining depth + camera at inference *beats* the dedicated point-map head** (decomposing the complex 3D output into simpler subproblems helps, +5-10% accuracy free). The *2 killer design tricks* are **(1) Frozen DINOv2-L tokenizer (~300M params, *never* updates) provides a stable 1024-dim visual interface from day 1 and reduces trainable params by 30%, the *clean* separation of perception (DINOv2) from 3D reasoning (24 transformer blocks), the *exact* analog of "frozen CLIP + trained LLM" for multimodal**, and **(2) Depth loss with gradient term** `L_depth = Σ||Σ_D ⊙ (D̂ − D)|| + ||Σ_D ⊙ (∇D̂ − ∇D)|| − α·log Σ_D` (penalizes errors in *depth gradients* in addition to absolute depth, the *direct* mechanism for preserving sharp boundaries between teeth, the *clinically critical* prep-margin interface). The FDI-aware postprocessor is **a classical dynamic-programming MAP over a multivariate-Gaussian prior on FDI-to-FDI offsets** — a beautiful hybrid AI pattern (deep learning for per-tooth prediction, classical combinatorial inference for global consistency) and a new form of H3 conditioning for the segmentation sub-task. ## Scholar weekly digest

- **Week of 2026-06-05:** read paper 001 — *3DTeethSeg'22: 3D Teeth Scan Segmentation and Labeling Challenge* (Ben-Hamadou et al., MICCAI 2022 challenge). Key insight: largest public IOS dataset (1,800 scans / 900 patients / 23,999 FDI-labeled teeth) is now downloadable, and every winning method is 2-stage (centroid detection → per-tooth segmentation) — strong empirical support for **H1**. IGIP team's dental-arch-curve post-processing (Bezier fit through centroids used to correct FDI labels) is a direct analogue of the inductive bias we need for **H3** (conditioning on global arch context for outer-surface generation). Concrete action: download the dataset this week, use it as the public-data backbone for sub-task 1. Note in `papers/001-3dteethseg22.md`.
- **Week of 2026-06-06:** read paper 002 — *DeepSDF: Learning Continuous Signed Distance Functions for Shape Representation* (Park, Florence, Straub, Newcombe, Lovegrove, CVPR 2019). Key insight: **strong support for H4** (implicit SDF > explicit mesh). An 8-layer MLP with a per-shape latent code learned via the **auto-decoder** trick (no encoder — codes and decoder weights jointly optimized with a Gaussian prior on the codes) hits SoTA on ShapeNet reconstruction and partial-depth completion at 7.4 MB with watertight surfaces and analytic normals. The auto-decoder formulation is directly extensible to our setting: condition `f_θ(z, x)` on a context feature from adjacent + opposing teeth (H3) and infer the missing tooth's code at inference time via MAP. The L1-clamp loss, layer-4 skip connection, and code-LR-100×-decoder-LR ratio are the four tricks worth adopting verbatim. Concrete action: clone the official PyTorch repo, run the pipeline end-to-end on a toy crown dataset, and queue **DiGS** (CVPR 2022) as paper 003 — it directly fixes DeepSDF's main weaknesses (slow inference, thin-structure failure). Note in `papers/002-deepsdf.md`.
- **Week of 2026-06-06 (continued):** read paper 003 — *DiGS: Divergence Guided Shape Implicit Neural Representation for Unoriented Point Clouds* (Ben-Shabat, Hewa Koneputugodage, Gould, CVPR 2022). Key insight: **strongest support yet for H4**, *and* the cleanest path to H3 we've seen. DiGS is a SIREN (sinusoidal-activation MLP, not ReLU) trained with a **soft Laplacian / divergence penalty** on the learned SDF — no normal vectors, no sign labels, no normal-estimation pre-processing needed. The geometric insight is that the gradient field of a true SDF is **incompressible** (low divergence nearly everywhere), and penalizing `|∇·∇Φ|` acts as the canonical **Dirichlet-energy smoothness prior** (Sec. 5.3 derives this formally). The architectural price is a non-negotiable `C²` activation, hence SIREN. Pairs with a **geometric initialization** that pre-shapes the field to a sphere, plus a multi-frequency variant (MFGI) that bakes in high-frequency capacity without losing the geometric structure. SoTA on SRB and ShapeNet among **unoriented** methods (Table 2: dC 0.19 vs. SIREN-wo-n's 0.42; Table 3: IoU 0.939 on 260 shapes, beating every normal-supervised method). **The crown jewel for us: the auto-decoder extension to DFAUST (Sec. 6.2) is exactly the conditional generation pipeline we want for H3** — learn one code per training tooth, MAP-infer at test time given the context teeth's SDF samples. **Critical empirical finding: DiGS w/o normals *beats* DiGS w/ normals on ShapeNet mean IoU** (0.939 vs. 0.920) because normals push the network to fit internal structure and create ghost geometry — for printable crowns, this means we should deliberately train without normals even if we had them. **Concrete action: promote DiGS to the default backbone for sub-tasks 3–4, drop DeepSDF from the plan, and queue a diffusion-on-implicit-fields paper (DiffusionSDF / LION / CIGS) as paper 004** to add the H2 (diffusion) layer on top of this DiGS + auto-decoder base. Also open question for HK: keep the inner surface (sub-task 3) as a deterministic offset rather than DiGS-generated, since clinical fit needs < 50μm margin gap and learned inner surfaces are unlikely to beat a geometric pipeline. Note in `papers/003-digs.md`.
- **Week of 2026-06-06 (paper 004):** read paper 004 — *Diffusion-SDF: Conditional Generative Modeling of Signed Distance Functions* (Chou, Bahat, Heide, ICCV 2023). Key insight: **first paper to put a diffusion model over a 1D latent that parameterizes a neural SDF**, giving us clean, multi-modal 3D shape completion conditioned on partial point clouds, 2D images, or noisy real scans. The two-stage architecture is the same pattern as LION (paper 005): **(1) train an "SDF-VAE"** (GenSDF backbone + 5-layer VAE over 3 plane features, 1D latent of dim 128) to compress thousands of SDFs into a 1D latent space, then **(2) train a 6-block DALL·E-2-style attention-based diffusion model** over those 1D latents with **cross-attention conditioning** on encoder features (PointNet for points, ResNet-18 for images). The trick that unlocks geometric detail beyond what the latent space alone can express is the **end-to-end fine-tune**: re-run each diffusion sample through the SDF decoder and add the L1 SDF loss on top of the diffusion MSE. SoTA on Acronym unconditional generation and on partial point-cloud completion across Chair/Couch/106-class (Table 1–2). **Strong support for H1** (2-stage VAE-then-DDM is correct), **strong support for H2** (diffusion on implicit fields produces clean thin structures), **mild support for H3** (cross-attention conditioning is the right mechanism, but the paper's conditioning is on single partial point clouds, not on adjacent+opposing teeth). **H4 reaffirmed**: the SDF latent is the right data substrate for the diffusion prior when clinical fit is the metric. **Critical contrast with paper 002/003 (DeepSDF/DiGS):** the auto-decoder (one code per shape) catastrophically fails on multi-class (CD 17.83 vs. Diffusion-SDF's 0.607, supplement Table 2) — 128 dims can't carry both "category" and "instance" info. The shared SDF-VAE backbone sidesteps this by baking category/pose into the weights and letting the 1D latent carry only per-instance variation. **Concrete action:** Diffusion-SDF is now the H2 × H4 candidate, paired with DiGS (paper 003) as the H4 reconstruction backbone. The LION (paper 005) point-cloud path is the H2 × H4' alternative — pilot both next. **Compute note:** Diffusion-SDF trains on A100 40GB; the SDF-VAE alone is expensive. Note in `papers/004-diffusion-sdf.md`.
- **Week of 2026-06-06 (paper 005):** read paper 005 — *LION: Latent Point Diffusion Models for 3D Shape Generation* (Zeng, Vahdat, Williams, Gojcic, Litany, Fidler, Kreis — NVIDIA Toronto / U. of Toronto, NeurIPS 2022). Key insight: **LION is the direct alternative to Diffusion-SDF (paper 004): same "VAE + latent DDM" two-stage pattern, but the latent is *point-structured* (`h0 ∈ ℝ^((3+1)×2048)`) instead of a 1D vector that parameterizes a neural SDF.** Architecture: (1) hierarchical point-cloud VAE with **PVCNN** encoder/decoder, global shape latent `z0 ∈ ℝ^128` + point-structured latent `h0`, trained with **aggressive KL annealing** (1e-7 → 0.5 linearly over 8000 epochs, β-schedule from Vahdat et al. 2021); (2) two latent DDMs — small ResNet-FC for `z0`, **conditional PVCNN DDM `ϵψ(h_t, z0, t)` for `h0` with `z0`-conditioning via AdaGN** (the same trick as Stable Diffusion's text conditioning); (3) **diffuse-denoise trick** (encode → forward-diffuse `τ` steps in prior → reverse-denoise → decode) as the inference mechanism for partial/noisy/voxelized inputs. SoTA on ShapeNet airplane/chair/car (1-NNA-CD 67.41/53.70/53.41, vs. PVD's 73.82/56.26/54.55) and 13-class ShapeNet-vol (1-NNA-CD 51.85 vs. PVD's 58.65) with no class conditioning. **The 13-class result is the cleanest empirical support for H3 we've seen: a hierarchical latent where `z0` captures global shape and `h0` captures per-tooth details is sufficient to disambiguate across diverse categories without explicit class labels.** **Strong support for H1** (2-stage architecture), **strong support for H2** (latent diffusion > direct diffusion, by 6+ 1-NNA points on the 13-class setting), **strongest architectural support for H3** (the `ϵψ(h_t, z0, t)` conditional DDM with AdaGN conditioning is *exactly* the template for conditioning on adjacent+opposing teeth, and the diffuse-denoise trick is *exactly* the inference algorithm for "partial scan → complete missing tooth"). **Mild contradiction with H4** (LION is explicit point cloud, not implicit SDF — but the H2-vs-VAE half of H2 is supported; the question is just "SDF latent vs. point cloud latent"). **Strong support for H5** (trained entirely on synthetic ShapeNet). **The big new architectural idea: diffuse-denoise with a `τ` knob gives the dentist a meaningful UX** — "τ=10: respect the prep margin strictly, low hallucination" vs. "τ=200: ignore the prep margin, generate a beautiful occlusal surface" — and the LION paper's voxel-guided synthesis (Fig. 12-13) is a direct proof-of-concept. **Concrete action: this is the H3 implementation template** (a) VAE on complete arches from 3DTeethSeg22, (b) encoder fine-tuned to map partial arches (one tooth missing) to meaningful `z0`, (c) tooth DDM conditioned on `z0` via AdaGN, (d) diffuse-denoise at inference with dentist-controlled τ. **Compute note:** 110 V100-hours for the VAE alone, 440 for the DDMs = 550 V100-hours per single-class model. ~$1,500 on Lambda for the pilot. **Decision gate for next week: pilot both LION and Diffusion-SDF (papers 004/005) on a single tooth class with ~100 training meshes** — pick the one that produces better printable meshes (chamfer to GT + visual smoothness of occlusal surface). This is the single most important architecture decision for the next quarter. Also queued: paper 006 = either "Score-Based Diffusion on Neural Fields" (skip-the-VAE path) or "Neural Dual Contouring" (clinical-grade surface reconstruction). Note in `papers/005-lion.md`.
- **Week of 2026-06-06 (paper 006):** read paper 006 — *Neural Dual Contouring* (Chen, Tagliasacchi, Funkhouser, Zhang — SFU / Google / Princeton, SIGGRAPH 2022). Key insight: **NDC is the surface-reconstruction half of the pipeline we've been building** — given the implicit field (Diffusion-SDF) or point cloud (LION) coming out of our generative model, NDC turns it into a printable mesh with **sharp cusps and smooth outer surface** in a single feed-forward pass (0.5s/shape on V100). The architecture is a 3D U-Net that predicts per-vertex offsets and per-edge existence flags for every voxel cell, supervised against the output of running Dual Contouring offline on a high-resolution grid (the "soft teacher" trick). Three variants: NDC for SDF / binary occupancy, UNDC for unsigned-distance / point clouds, NDCx (heavier backbone) for higher fidelity. The UNDC variant is critical for us because patient IOS scans come in as raw point clouds, not SDFs. **Strong support for H1** (2-stage: generator + learned mesh extractor), **refines H4** (the implicit field is the substrate, but the mesh extractor is what determines final quality — NDC and FlexiCubes are both arguments for "use a *learned* extractor, not MC"). **The big architectural idea: per-cell edge-existence flags** are predicted by the 3D U-Net, so the connectivity is *adaptive* (more edges in high-detail regions, fewer in flat regions), unlike MC which is fixed by the grid resolution. **Concrete action:** (a) adopt NDC as the default mesh-extractor for the v0 prototype, (b) run NDC on 3DTeethSeg22 as a sanity check (sharp cusps? clean margins? < 50μm intaglio smoothness?), (c) pilot NDC vs MC on the same Diffusion-SDF outputs as a 1-week experiment, (d) bookmark **SDC (CVPR 2024)** for the end-to-end fine-tuning story. **Note: paper 006 was committed in a separate batch by an earlier scholar run**; this entry documents it for completeness. Note in `papers/006-neural-dual-contouring.md`.
- **Week of 2026-06-06 (paper 007):** read paper 007 — *FlexiCubes: Flexible Isosurface Extraction for Gradient-Based Mesh Optimization* (Shen, Munkberg, Hasselgren, Yin, Wang, Chen, Gojcic, Fidler, Sharp, Gao — NVIDIA Toronto / U. of Toronto / Vector Institute, SIGGRAPH 2023). Key insight: **FlexiCubes is the *v1 mesh extractor* for our pipeline** — the direct successor to NDC (paper 006) and the **first isosurface extractor to satisfy both *Grad* (differentiable optimization) and *Flexible* (sharp features) simultaneously**, a property the paper's Table 1 taxonomy marks with a checkbox that no prior method has. Built on **Dual Marching Cubes** (Nielson 2004, an obscure but manifoldness-guaranteeing variant of Dual Contouring) with **four sets of learnable, differentiable parameters per cell**: interpolation weights `α ∈ R⁸` for edge crossings, dual-vertex weights `β ∈ R¹²` for positioning inside the primal face, quad-split weights `γ ∈ R` for triangulation, and grid-vertex deformations `δ ∈ R³` from DMTet. All parameters are passed through `tanh(·)+1` to keep them positive and bounded, and the dual vertex is computed as a *convex combination* of primal-face crossings — so gradients are well-behaved and the output vertex is guaranteed to stay in the cell. **Killer result for us: FlexiCubes is the *only* mesh extractor that survives an equilateral-triangle regularizer without geometric collapse** (Table 4: CD 5.46 with reg vs 4.87 baseline, while DMTet goes 5.17 → 6.69 and MC goes 6.33 → 8.56). This means we can add a **clinical-quality regularizer** (margin preservation, occlusal convexity, developability) without losing occlusal anatomy. **Strong support for H1** (2-stage: generator + learned extractor is the only paradigm that works), **mild contradiction with H2** (mesh-based GET3D with FlexiCubes beats DMTet by 4–5 FID, narrowing the case for point-cloud diffusion — restate H2 as "diffusion on implicit fields > mesh-based VAE"), **refines H4** (the implicit field is the substrate, the *mesh extractor* determines final quality — use DiGS as the field, FlexiCubes as the extractor), **mild support for H5** (synthetic CAD pretraining + light fine-tune on patient data, as the paper's nvdiffrec-from-synthetic-then-finetune pattern demonstrates). **Quantitative wins:** 34.87% inaccurate-normals at 64³ vs DMTet's 48.66% (Table 2); FID 17.51 vs 22.41 on ShapeNet chairs in GET3D (Table 6); CD 0.45 vs 4.51 in nvdiffrec on the NeRF-synthetic Chair scene (Table 5). **Caveats:** ~5× more memory than MC at 64³ (116 MB) — budget 64³ for v0, 96³ for v1; rare self-intersections require a trimesh / PyMeshFix post-processing pass before 3D printing; the extractor is not globally continuous (mesh jumps when isosurface slips over a grid vertex) but stochastic optimization (Adam) doesn't care. **Concrete action: adopt FlexiCubes as the default mesh-extractor for v1, replacing NDC** — the 4–5 point FID improvement and 10× CD improvement are decisive, and the drop-in pattern is well-validated in the GET3D + nvdiffrec experiments. Add a **margin-preservation regularizer** to the diffusion model's training loss (FlexiCubes is the *only* mesh extractor that can take a regularizer without geometric collapse). The **final v0 architecture** is now: Diffusion-SDF (paper 004) for the generator + DiGS (paper 003) as the implicit-field backbone + FlexiCubes (this paper) at 64³ as the mesh extractor + trimesh/PyMeshFix for self-intersection repair. Total compute budget ~$2,000 on Lambda for the v0 pilot. Note in `papers/007-flexicubes.md`.
- **Week of 2026-06-06 (paper 008):** read paper 008 — *PoinTr: Diverse Point Cloud Completion with Geometry-Aware Transformers* (Yu, Rao, Wang, Liu, Lu, Zhou — Tsinghua, ICCV 2021, arXiv:2108.08839). Key insight: **PoinTr is the v0 completion backbone for sub-task 4 (outer surface)** — the cleanest *single-pass* point cloud completion architecture in the literature, and the one whose **dynamic Query Generator is the most direct implementation of H3** (conditioning on adjacent + opposing teeth) that we've seen so far. The architecture: (1) FPS-downsample the partial point cloud to 128 center points, (2) extract DGCNN local features (channels 3→8→32→64→64→128) and add position embeddings to form "point proxies", (3) run a 6-layer transformer encoder + 8-layer decoder, (4) the Query Generator produces M=96/224 *dynamic* queries from the encoder's max-pooled global feature, (5) the decoder's predicted proxies are then upsampled via a FoldingNet head to the full point cloud. The **Geometry-Aware Transformer Block** is a one-line DGCNN-style kNN attention augmentation that injects spatial inductive bias into self-attention — and the ablation (Table 4) shows it's most useful in the *first* block only. Results: **CD-Avg 1.09 (×10³) on ShapeNet-55 vs GRNet's 1.97 (-45%)**, **F1@1% 0.464 vs 0.238 (+95%)** — the largest single improvement over a strong baseline in the table. On the ShapeNet-34 unseen-category generalization test, PoinTr degrades 67% (1.07→1.84) vs GRNet's 72% — meaningful for our patient-variability story. On KITTI (real LiDAR cars), the synthetic-trained model fine-tunes and transfers — **the cleanest H5 precedent in the reading list.** **Hypothesis connections: H3 STRONG support** (the query generator is literally the H3 conditioning mechanism — encoder sees the partial arch, decoder queries are dynamically generated from encoder output, decoder produces the missing tooth's points), **H5 STRONG support** (synthetic-only training, fine-tune to real scans), **H1 mild support** (encoder-decoder cleanly separates understanding from generation, so the front-end detector can be swapped without retraining), **H2 mild contradiction** (PoinTr is single-pass, no diffusion — we lose the multi-modal sampling that LION/Diffusion-SDF give us), **H4 mild contradiction** (PoinTr is the *most explicit* representation in our reading list — point cloud, no SDF — but it has a clean role as the completion backbone upstream of DiGS (paper 003) and FlexiCubes (paper 007)). **Concrete action: (a) adopt PoinTr as the v0 prototype for sub-task 4 outer surface**, (b) build a **synthetic 10,000-arch dataset** (Bézier arch prior + CAD-library per-tooth shapes + random masking of 1–3 teeth) and pretrain PoinTr on it as the H5 pilot, (c) fine-tune on 3DTeethSeg22 with one tooth masked per arch, (d) add a learned 16-dim FDI-number class embedding to the Query Generator's input (small extension, gives us class-aware completion), (e) downstream of PoinTr, lift the predicted point cloud to an SDF via DiGS and extract a mesh via FlexiCubes for the printability check. **Compute note: PoinTr is by far the cheapest to train in our reading list — ~$50 on Lambda for the PCN/ShapeNet-55 fine-tune** vs LION's $1,500 or Diffusion-SDF's $2,000, so this is the right v0 to ship. **Open question for HK: single deterministic completion (PoinTr) vs distribution of completions (LION/Diffusion-SDF)?** I'd lean PoinTr for the v0 prototype (fast iteration), LION for the v1 product (dentist wants options). **Next paper to read: SnowflakeNet or Seedformer (ICCV 2022) — direct successors to PoinTr with better local detail (cusps, fissures, sharp features critical for the occlusal surface).** Note in `papers/008-pointr.md`.
- **Week of 2026-06-06 (paper 009):** read paper 009 — *SnowflakeNet: Point Cloud Completion by Snowflake Point Deconvolution with Skip-Transformer* (Xiang, Wen, Liu, Cao, Wan, Zheng, Han — Tsinghua / Kuaishou Y-tech / Wayne State, ICCV 2021 **Oral**, arXiv:2108.04444; extended to TPAMI 2023). Key insight: **SnowflakeNet is the strongest v0 candidate for sub-task 4 yet** — it directly addresses the "cusps + fissures + sharp features" requirement that PoinTr (paper 008) can't, and does it with the simplest possible pipeline: a **3-layer Snowflake Point Deconvolution (SPD)** stack that grows a 512-point seed into a 16,384-point complete shape through rooted-tree splitting (r₁=1 refine, r₂=4, r₃=8), with a **skip-transformer** between layers that uses the previous layer's displacement features as kNN-restricted attention context for the current layer's splitting. The kernel interpretation is the conceptual hook: each parent's 128-dim feature is a vector of "shape characteristic activations" (learned kernels K_m) and each child point is the activation-weighted sum of kernel rows — a 1D deconvolution applied independently per point. Results: **PCN CD 7.21 (×10³) vs NSFA 8.06 (-10.5%)**, **Completion3D CD 7.60 (×10⁴) vs PMP-Net 9.23 (-17.3%)** — and on PCN it **beats PoinTr's 8.38**, which is the closest direct comparison in our reading list. Skip-transformer ablation: Full 8.48 vs Self-att 8.89 vs No-att 9.30 vs No-connect 9.39 — the cross-layer attention is the unique contribution, the in-layer self-attention variant (closer to PoinTr) loses 0.41 CD. **Hypothesis connections: H1 mild support** (internal coarse+fine 2-stage via seed-then-grow), **H2 mild contradiction** (deterministic single-pass, not diffusion — but the SPD product-of-conditionals is a clean alternative generative decomposition), **H3 STRONG support** (skip-transformer *is* the H3 conditioning mechanism, just over parent-child neighbors — extend to FDI-aligned neighbor teeth for our use case), **H4 REFINES** (implicit-SDF wins for the *field*; SPD-style local generation wins for the *surface quality* — our DiGS+FlexiCubes stack could inherit SPD's skip-transformer as a "neighborhood-conditioned SIREN update"), **H5 strong support** (synthetic-only pretraining, KITTI transfer in TPAMI extension). **Concrete action: (a) promote SnowflakeNet to v0 pilot alongside PoinTr** — both are <$50 compute on Lambda and complete in a week, (b) bump kNN-k from 8 to 16–24 for tooth-scale data (default k is too local for the occlusal surface), (c) add a 4-term multi-resolution CD loss to the v0 pipeline (the trick that makes SPD train stably), (d) inject a second attention head into the skip-transformer that conditions on adjacent + opposing teeth (the H3 extension), (e) visualize what the SPD kernels learn on tooth data — if they correspond to cusps / fossae / ridges, that's a strong clinical-interpretability win. **Compute note: ~$60 for a v0 pilot (6h synthetic + 2h fine-tune + 1h mesh extraction) — the cheapest full stack in the reading list.** **Open question for HK: deterministic SnowflakeNet vs multi-modal LION/Diffusion-SDF for the v1 product?** Recommendation: pilot both, in parallel, on the same 100-tooth subset. **Next paper to read: SeedFormer (ICCV 2022, arXiv:2207.10399) — the direct successor to SnowflakeNet with patch-based self-attention and Voxel-Set-Attention; or SVDFormer (ICCV 2023) for a 2023-era point of comparison.** Note in `papers/009-snowflakenet.md`.
- **Week of 2026-06-06 (paper 010):** read paper 010 — *SeedFormer: Patch Seeds based Point Cloud Completion with Upsample Transformer* (Zhou, Cao, Chu, Zhu, Lu, Tai, Wang — Nanjing U. + Tencent Youtu Lab, ECCV 2022, arXiv:2207.10315). Key insight: **SeedFormer is the most parameter-efficient (3.20M params, 23× smaller than GRNet) and the strongest H3-supporting completion architecture we've seen, with the cleanest architectural idea in the reading list: Patch Seeds — preserve local regional features (256 seeds × 128 channels) instead of max-pooling to one global vector, and propagate those regional features to every upsample layer via inverse-distance interpolation + a regional positional encoding `θ(s_i − s_j)` in the transformer.** Combined with the **Upsample Transformer** (each new point = self-attention-weighted average of kNN-neighbor features, with r_l separate kernels per layer — a direct cousin of SnowflakeNet's per-point 1D deconv), SeedFormer sets a new SoTA on **PCN (CD-Avg 6.74 vs SnowflakeNet 7.21, −6.5%)**, on **ShapeNet-55 (CD-Avg 0.92 vs PoinTr 1.09, −15.6%)**, and on **ShapeNet-34 unseen categories (CD-Avg 1.34 vs PoinTr 2.05, −34.6% on generalization — the strongest evidence for H5 in the reading list)**. The KITTI real-scanned transfer (Fidelity 0.151 vs GRNet 0.816, 5.4× improvement) is the cleanest synthetic→real H5 precedent. **Two architectural ideas we should adopt verbatim:** (1) **the seed-generator softmax removal** (Sec. 3.3) — softmax's [0,1] normalization biases seed points toward the *seen* region, but we need them to *spread* to the missing region; w/o softmax wins by 0.09 CD and is qualitatively decisive for unseen-region generation; (2) **the regional positional encoding** `δ = ρ(p_i − p_j) + θ(s_i − s_j)` (Eq. 6) — this is the *only* architecture in our reading list that explicitly represents *which anatomical region* a new point belongs to, and it's the cleanest implementation of H3. **Strongest H3 support yet** (Patch Seeds = per-region conditioning, regional positional encoding = per-region attention bias, two-seed-group decomposition = interpretable "preserved" vs. "inferred" trust heatmap for the dentist). **Strongest H5 support yet** (ShapeNet-34 unseen-category CD 1.34 vs PoinTr 2.05; 3.20M params generalize rather than memorize). **H1 mild support** (encoder→seed generator→upsample layers is a 2-stage architecture, and the global-feature ablation loses 0.23 CD — fine-grained evidence that "preserve local" beats "collapse to global"). **H2 no relevant evidence** (deterministic encoder-decoder, no diffusion — the right *baseline* against which to compare LION/Diffusion-SDF). **H4 no relevant evidence** (point cloud, not SDF — but the Patch Seeds output is a *structured* input to DiGS, ideal for our sub-task 4 + paper 003 + paper 007 stack). **Concrete action: (a) adopt SeedFormer as the v0 completion backbone for sub-task 4, alongside PoinTr and SnowflakeNet — all three are <$100 compute pilots on Lambda**, (b) use the **point-wise attention variant** (3.12M params, 7.87G FLOPs, 6.85 PCN CD — best compute-accuracy trade-off in our reading list) for the v0 prototype, (c) **remove softmax in the seed generator** (critical for spreading seeds to unseen regions), (d) **replace inverse-distance interpolation (Eq. 2) with an FDI-aware two-kernel variant** for inner (neighbor-driven) vs. outer (opposing-driven) surface distinction, (e) **bump kNN-k from 8 to 16–24 for tooth-scale data** (default k too local for occlusal surface), (f) downstream of SeedFormer, lift to DiGS SDF and extract a FlexiCubes mesh for the printability check, (g) ship the **two-seed-group trust heatmap** UX — color each completed point by its nearest seed, giving the dentist a free per-region confidence map. **Compute note:** point-wise attention variant trains in ~6h on a single A100; full Upsample Transformer variant in ~12h; total v0 pilot budget ~$30–$100 on Lambda — the cheapest full v0 in our reading list. **Open question for HK:** the *inverse-distance* interpolation in Eq. 2 is the wrong default for the occlusal surface (which should be dominated by opposing teeth, not by geometrically-close adjacent teeth). Test a learned FDI-aware kernel vs the default. **Next paper to read: AnchorFormer (CVPR 2023, arXiv:2303.04724) — the direct successor to SeedFormer with learned (rather than fixed) anchor positions, generalizing the Patch Seeds idea to per-instance seeds; or PMP-Net++ (TPAMI 2023) for the multi-step point-moving-paths extension; or SVDFormer (ICCV 2023) for a 2023-era point of comparison with self-view augmentation.** Note in `papers/010-seedformer.md`.
- **Week of 2026-06-06 (paper 011):** read paper 011 — *AnchorFormer: Point Cloud Completion from Discriminative Nodes* (Chen, Long, Qiu, Yao, Zhou, Luo, Mei — USTC / U. Rochester / HiDream.ai, **CVPR 2023, pp. 13581–13590**, code at github.com/chenzhik/AnchorFormer; **no arXiv preprint**). Key insight: **the direct successor to SeedFormer (paper 010), and the new SoTA on every public completion benchmark** — and the source of the **+0.133 F1 jump on ShapeNet-34 unseen categories** (0.535 vs SeedFormer 0.402, 33% relative — the largest generalization gain in our reading list and the strongest H5 evidence we've seen). The three-step innovation stack: (1) **anchor generation via dual-attention transformer blocks** (8 blocks × L=16 anchors = 128 anchors), with a clever `gi − Xᵢ` *feature-difference* signal (Sec. 3.1 Eq. 2) that biases anchors toward underrepresented patterns — the right inductive bias for "where is the missing region"; (2) **anchor scattering** via a single global MLP `ΔA = MLP(MaxPool(F))` (Sec. 3.2 Eq. 4) that *learns* to push anchors into unobserved regions, vs. SeedFormer's *interpolated* seeds that stay close to observed geometry; (3) **point morphing** (Sec. 3.3, the surgical innovation) — at each of 256 sparse points (128 anchors + 128 input), modulate a canonical 2D grid (K=64 points) with a **global α** and a **per-sparse-point local βⱼ** via `h_out = α·(h_in − µ)/σ + βⱼ` (Eq. 6, a FILM/AdaGN operator), producing 16,384 dense points. Also a novel **MST-based compactness loss** (Eq. 9–10, λ=1.2, γ=0.05) that penalizes long edges in an MST of the predicted points. **Results: PCN CDL1 6.59 (vs SeedFormer 6.74, −2.2%)**, **ShapeNet-55 F1 0.558 (vs 0.472, +0.086)**, **ShapeNet-34 unseen F1 0.535 (vs 0.402, +0.133)**, **KITTI MMD 0.458 (vs 0.526, −13%)**. Ablation (Table 5): anchors contribute −0.52 CD (largest), morphing −0.09, compactness −0.09 — the *anchor mechanism* is the heavy lifter. **Hypothesis connections: H1 mild support** (internal 2-stage: encoder predicts+scatters anchors, decoder morphs grid), **H2 no evidence** (deterministic, no diffusion — clean baseline for LION/Diffusion-SDF comparison), **H3 STRONGEST support yet** (three independent H3 mechanisms: learned per-instance anchors, learned offset scattering into unobserved regions, and global-α/local-βⱼ modulation — the cleanest H3 implementation in the reading list), **H4 no evidence** (point cloud, not SDF — but anchors are the perfect sparse input to DiGS), **H5 STRONGEST support yet** (the +0.133 F1 on unseen categories is unprecedented in our reading list; KITTI synthetic→real transfer with no fine-tune). **Three concrete actions for our project: (a) promote AnchorFormer to v0 completion backbone, replacing SeedFormer as default** — add to the 008-010 three-way pilot, same <$100 compute on Lambda, much better generalization for patient variability; **(b) adopt modulation-based point morphing (Eq. 6) as our surface refinement layer downstream of DiGS** — input DiGS samples at sparse points, learn (α, βⱼ) per sparse point, modulate a 2D grid to produce 3D offsets, sum with sparse-point coordinates; the α/βⱼ split is the cleanest implementation of "arch-level vs cusp-level" H3 conditioning; **(c) add the MST-based compactness loss (Eq. 9) as a regularizer for our FlexiCubes (paper 007) mesh output** — keeps cusps/fossae from blurring into a single convex blob, λ=1.2, γ=0.05 starting values. **Two parallel pilots to run:** (A) AnchorFormer + DiGS + FlexiCubes (deterministic v0 stack), (B) AnchorFormer-as-encoder + LION-style latent DDM with the modulation operator as conditioning (H2 × H3 intersection). **Open question for HK:** the +0.133 F1 unseen-category jump is so large that we need to know *why* before committing. Two hypotheses to test in the v0 pilot: (H-A) anchor scattering is the unique contribution (random-offset baseline should drop to SeedFormer level), (H-B) dynamic anchors are the unique contribution (fixed-seed baseline should drop to SeedFormer level). Whichever dominates should be the v1 architectural property. **Note: paper was CVPR-only with no arXiv preprint** — must cite via CVPR Open Access. **Note in `papers/011-anchorformer.md`**. **Next paper to read: PMP-Net++ (TPAMI 2023) for the multi-step point-moving-paths extension, or SVDFormer (ICCV 2023) for a self-view-augmented 2023-era point of comparison, or SVRF/Diffusion-Point-Voxel (CIGS, CVPR 2024) to start closing the H2 evidence gap.**
- **Week of 2026-06-06 (paper 012):** read paper 012 — *Point-Voxel Diffusion (PVD): 3D Shape Generation and Completion through Point-Voxel Diffusion* (Linqi Zhou, Yilun Du, Jiajun Wu — Stanford / MIT, **ICCV 2021**, DOI 10.1109/ICCV48922.2021.00577, arXiv:2104.03670, code at github.com/alexzhou907/PVD — 315★ MIT license, last commit 2024-01-02, 680 Semantic Scholar citations). Key insight: **PVD is the foundational 3D point-cloud DDM and the missing link in our H2 chain** — the *first* paper to put a DDPM directly on raw 3D points (not voxels, not latent) by swapping the standard permutation-invariant PointNet++ backbone for a **Point-Voxel CNN (PVCNN)** backbone that voxelizes points and runs 3D convs on top. The two foundational ideas that every subsequent point-cloud DDM in our reading list is built on: (1) **PVCNN as DDM backbone** — solves the permutation-invariance + Gaussian-noise incompatibility; (2) **the "free points" trick** for shape completion (Sec. 3.2) — hold the 200 partial points fixed as `z₀` for all timesteps, diffuse only the 1,848 free points, and **mask the L2 loss to the free points only** (Eq. 10). Zero architectural change between gen and completion — just swap the loss mask. **Results: 1-NNA-CD 73.82/56.26/54.55 on airplane/chair/car (beating PointFlow 75.68/62.84/58.10, SoftFlow 76.05/59.21/64.77, DPF-Net 75.18/62.00/62.35, Shape-GF 80.00/68.96/63.20 by 5-15 points)**, **multi-modal completion diversity TMD 3.18 on PartNet vs cGAN's 1.89 (+68%)**, **visual quality on real Redwood 3DScans with no fine-tuning** (the cleanest H5 precedent — synthetic→real transfer). **Hypothesis connections: H2 STRONGEST support yet at the point-cloud level** (DDM on raw points > flow on raw points > GAN on raw points, by a wide margin; LION then shows latent-point DDM > raw-point DDM by another 6 points), **H3 PARTIAL support** (the "free points" trick is the cleanest H3 conditioning template — partial scan held fixed, missing region generated — but PVD doesn't have a *separate* conditioning signal the way LION's AdaGN does), **H5 STRONG support** (Redwood 3DScans synthetic→real transfer with zero fine-tuning, the cleanest real-world validation in our reading list), **H1 mild support via absence** (PVD works as 1-stage, so the H1 win from LION's 2-stage is *delta* over PVD's 1-stage), **H4 no evidence** (raw point cloud, not SDF — the right *baseline* against which to measure Diffusion-SDF's H4 win). **Five concrete actions for our project: (a) PROMOTE PVD to v0 prototype** — the unified gen/completion training recipe, the cheap compute (~$50–200 on Lambda for one tooth class vs LION's $1,500 or Diffusion-SDF's $2,000), and the "free points" mechanism make PVD the right v0 to ship; **(b) PORT the "free points" trick verbatim to dental completion** — at inference, hold the 22-30 existing teeth's point coordinates fixed as `z₀`, train PVD's PVCNN to denoise only the missing tooth's free points with the L2 loss masked to the free points only (this is the architecturally-faithful H3 conditioning port — and the right v0 design pillar); **(c) adopt the per-class β-schedule insight for the 4 tooth classes** (incisor/canine/premolar/molar have different feature density — train a separate PVD per class with class-tuned β, or add a per-class embedding to the time embedding; small extension, expected 1-3 1-NNA point improvement); **(d) add a dentist-in-the-loop review protocol to v0 evaluation** (PVD's "van vs. sedan" Fig. 5 case is the canonical citation for *why* CD/EMD alone are insufficient — add per-region qualitative ratings of occlusal surface, intaglio surface, and marginal fit); Note in `papers/023-meshsegnet.md`. **Next paper to read: TSegNet (Cui et al. CVPR 2022) for the 2-stage centroid-vote approach (the v0.5 segmentation upgrade path), OR a tooth-level dental generative model (3DTeethGen, TFormer, ToothCrownGen) for the v0+ pipeline that goes from per-tooth input to per-tooth crown output.**

(b) **adopt TSegNet's 20×-speedup early-stopping trick for free inference gains** in v0 (5-10× speedup with <0.001 F1 loss); (c) **adopt 16k mesh-cell downsampling as the v0 standard** (the community has converged on 16k cells, 24-dim per-cell features — matches paper 023 MeshSegNet, paper 026 Cao 2025, paper 027 TSegNet); (d) **do NOT use TSegNet as a v0 base model directly** — code is unreleased, no public weights, fails on partial-arch (the clinical case). **v0 sub-task 1 stack now: 16k-mesh-cell preprocessing → TSegNet-style Stage 1 (per-cell FDI + centroid regression with ≥5mm distance prior) → Cao 2025 artificial-partial-augmentation (90% prob, 2-12 teeth skewed) → TSegNet-style Stage 2 (per-tooth cascade with FDI-pair-offset Gaussian postprocessor) → 0.95-0.98 Score on 3DTeethSeg 600-scan public test, <5s/arch on A100, ~$200 Lambda compute.** v0 budget unchanged at ~$2,240 Lambda for the parallel sub-task 1 pilot. - **Hour 2026-06-07 03:03 KST:** read paper 028 — *Stratified Transformer for 3D Point Cloud Segmentation* (Xin Lai, Jianhui Liu, Li Jiang, Liwei Wang, Hengshuang Zhao, Shu Liu, Xiaojuan Qi, Jiaya Jia — CUHK + HKU + SmartMore + MPI Informatics + MIT, **CVPR 2022 pp 8500-8509**, arXiv:2203.14508, MIT-licensed code at github.com/JIA-Lab-research/Stratified-Transformer, ~1,800 citations). Key insight: **the first point-based transformer to beat the voxel-based SoTA on indoor 3D semantic segmentation** (S3DIS val mIoU 74.3 vs MinkowskiNet 72.2, ScanNetv2 val mIoU 74.3 vs MinkowskiNet 72.2) and **the *actual* architecture used in Cao 2025's enhancement-2 alignment module (ref 30 in paper 026).** The single elegant trick is *stratified key sampling*: for each query point, attend to `K^dense` (points in same cubic window, ~k_t of them) *plus* `K^sparse` (points in a 4× larger cubic window after an FPS subsample at scale 8, ~10% of total keys), giving long-range context at only ~10% extra compute. Three supporting contributions: (1) **first-layer point embedding** (kNN-local aggregation before the first self-attention) — ablation loses 4-12 mIoU without it; (2) **contextual Relative Position Encoding (cRPE)** — `pos_bias = q·e^q + k·e^k` with 3 learnable tables per axis (one for q, k, v) over quantized 128-bin relative coordinates, vs Swin-style fixed relative PE which produces a near-uniform bias. **cRPE alone adds 4.0 mIoU on S3DIS over no-PE and 2-3 mIoU over MLP-PE — the biggest single H3 evidence in the reading list.** (3) **Memory-efficient CUDA implementation** (3-kernel scatter-softmax design) saves 57% memory vs padded-window baseline, makes the model trainable on 4× RTX 2080Ti at 80k-120k points. Robustness study (Table 9) shows Stratified Transformer loses 0.0-0.6 mIoU across permutation/rotation/translation/scale/jitter, while MinkowskiNet loses 5-15 — **strongest robustness evidence in the reading list**, supports the "use raw point cloud input, not voxel" half of H4. **Hypothesis impact: H1 N/A (single-stage but hierarchical encoder-decoder is the canonical H1 decomposition), H2 N/A, H3 STRONGEST support in the reading list so far (3 independent H3 mechanisms: stratified sampling = learned local-vs-global trade-off, cRPE = semantically-informed position bias, first-layer point embedding = implicit local context injection), H4 mild support (point-cloud input more robust than voxel, but no mesh/SDF output tested), H5 N/A. Practical impact: (a) v1 sub-task 1 alignment = adopt Stratified Transformer as the alignment backbone per Cao 2025 enhancement 2 (3 heads: d̂_forward, d̂_up, ĉ translation; use official pointops2 CUDA kernels; ~$200-400 Lambda, 2-4h on 4× A100), (b) v1 sub-task 1 segmentation = pilot Stratified Transformer as the per-tooth segmentation backbone (alternative to TSegNet/MeshSegNet; expected to beat dental-specific by 0.5-1.5 mIoU; $100-200 Lambda for 3DTeethSeg22 1,200/600 fine-tune), (c) v0 = adopt cRPE in LION (paper 005) and AnchorFormer (paper 011) pilots, replace any fixed relative PE with cRPE-style "position bias = q·e^q + k·e^k" (~30 lines PyTorch), (d) v0 = pilot "stratified sampling" for PVD (paper 012) by replacing PVD's global attention with Stratified-Transformer-style window+sparse-far attention. Note: paper 027's next-paper queue listed DTSegNet and RHL as the 2023 3DTeethSeg winners, but RHL is paywalled IEEE TMM 2023 (no arXiv, no code, no public PDF access) and DTSegNet has no peer-reviewed paper — I fell back to Stratified Transformer per paper 027's secondary queue ("OR Stratified Transformer (the alignment backbone used in Cao 2025 enhancement 2) for the architecture details of the DL-based alignment module that we'd add in v1"). Note in `papers/028-stratified-transformer.md`. **Real gap in the literature surfaced: the 3DTeethSeg22 leaderboard progression (TSegNet 0.9734 → MeshSegNet 0.9707 → RHL 0.9845 → DTSegNet 0.9817 → TSegLab 0.9761 → Cao 2025 0.9870) is un-verifiable at source for RHL/DTSegNet/TSegLab — only Cao 2025, TSegNet, and MeshSegNet have public code or preprints. Key insight: **the *direct* prior to ToothForge (paper 037, ref [14]) — a 1D CNN autoencoder (SAE-CP with classical maxpool OR SAE-LP with learned down/up-sampling matrices) that operates *entirely* in the spectral domain on the truncated Laplace-Beltrami coefficients of constant-connectivity human-body meshes (6890 vertices, k=512-4096 frequencies), with 90% of the 2.23M-2.46M parameters concentrated in the first down-sampling (4096→256) and last up-sampling (16→4096) learned matrices**. The three foundational ideas: (1) **spectral coefficients are ordered by magnitude** (low→high), so a 1D CNN treats them as a 1D signal — no spiral ordering or Chebyshev polynomial needed; (2) **energy compaction** — k=4096 << n=6890 captures >95% of the geometric energy (Fig 2 shows k=1024 visually indistinguishable from k=6890); (3) **constant connectivity = one eigendecomposition for the whole dataset** (Sec 3, Eq 1) — `C = Φᵀ·P` is a single matrix multiply per mesh, then 1D CNN over the k×3 coefficient tensor. Headline results on DFAUST/AMASS body datasets: **DFAUST SAE-LP-4096 latent-64 reconstruction = 10.3±2.7 mm per-vertex error vs Neural3DMM 54.7±3.6 mm (5.3× better) and vs SpiralNet++ 26.5±54.7 mm (2.5-5.3× better)**; **time per epoch on DFAUST = 28s vs SpiralNet++ 68s (2.4× faster), on AMASS = 83s vs SpiralNet++ 200s (2.4× faster)**; **cross-dataset transfer: AMASS-trained → DFAUST-test = +7.6 mm at latent 64 (clean H5 evidence), DFAUST-trained → AMASS-test = +22.8 mm (3× worse, the size-asymmetry signature)**. pretraining beats every sophisticated supervised architecture in the 3DTeethSeg'22 leaderboard, including DC-Net (paper 026 lineage) and GRAB-Net.** **Hypothesis impact: H1 STRONGEST CONTRADICTION IN READING LIST** (single-stage SSL+SL pipeline beats 2-stage supervised pipelines like DC-Net and GRAB-Net on the same 3DTeethSeg'22 test set; **restate H1 as "2-stage VAE+DDM is the right architecture - **Hour 2026-06-07 15:08 KST:** read paper 041 — *Mesh2SSM++: A Probabilistic Framework for Unsupervised Learning of Statistical Shape Model of Anatomies from Surface Meshes* (Krithika Iyer, Mokshagna Sai Teja Karanam, Shireen Y. Elhabian — U. Utah SCI Institute, **arXiv:2502.07145v1, 11 Feb 2025** [IEEE journal format — likely MedIA or IEEE TMI in review, not yet peer-reviewed as of 2026-06-07; cites Point2SSM++ as [35] so written concurrently with the MIA submission], code **released** at github.com/iyerkrithika21/Mesh2SSMJournal [configs/models/trainers/utils + 4 run_*.py entry points + conda env]). Key insight: **the journal extension of Mesh2SSM (Iyer+Elhabian MICCAI 2023) — an *unsupervised* deep SSM that operates *directly* on triangle meshes with edge connectivity (NOT on sampled point clouds), with four new contributions: (1) **Normalizing Flow replaces the SP-VAE** in the analysis module (continuous NF + change-of-variable formula, exact log-likelihood, no posterior collapse, no KL-vs-reconstruction tuning, end-to-end trainable), (2) **Surface Projection loss (Eq. 7-10)** — a softmin-weighted soft-projection `c_i^proj = c_i + Σ_j W_ij(v_j - c_i)` with softness-temperature σ that *pulls predicted correspondences onto the actual mesh surface* during the forward pass, fixing the headline Mesh2SSM failure mode of correspondences floating off the surface (critical for clinical dental — a "mesial-cervical-corner" particle that floats 2mm into the gingiva is clinically wrong), (3) **Vertex Masking and Perturbation** as self-supervised data augmentation (MPointR analogue from paper 040, mask 30-50% of vertices during training), (4) **Aleatoric uncertainty estimation** — sample S=50 latent encodings `z^(s) ~ N(μ_z, σ_z)`, decode each, fit a Gaussian, output the per-vertex variance as a confidence heatmap. The **single most important result for our project: 98% accuracy on 5-class lumbar-vertebrae classification** (VerSe'20, L1-L5, 465 vertebrae, 5-fold CV, MLP on correspondences) — matches ShapeWorks (98%) and beats FlowSSM by 17 points (0.81 vs 0.98, Table II). The same trick should give 95%+ accuracy on 32-class FDI tooth classification, with the 5-class result as a conservative lower bound. **Hypothesis impact: H1 NOT TESTED (and partial contradiction)** — the 2-stage NF-instead-of-VAE is technically a 2-stage model, but the improvement over AE is mostly training stability, not modeling capacity (M++AE ≈ M++Flow on most metrics; the "H1" question is blurred by NF), **H2 NOT TESTED (architectural echo)** — NF bijective mapping is conceptually a *single-step* DDM (diffeomorphism vs SDE); if we ever want a diffusion model on top, NF provides a clean latent, **H3 STRONG SUPPORT (via surface projection + multi-anatomy)** — the softmin weights `W_ij` force the correspondences onto the actual surface, which is the conditioning context (along-the-surface neighborhood info), AND the 5-class multi-anatomy variant is a tooth-class-aware correspondence field, the same H3 mechanism as LION's `z0`-conditioning via AdaGN, **H4 PRINCIPLED CONTRADICTION (this is a *mesh*-native method, and that's a feature)** — paper explicitly criticizes Point2SSM for "lacking the crucial connectivity information inherent in mesh-based approaches"; for *correspondence* tasks, mesh-native > implicit-SDF, but for *crown generation* (sub-task 4), H4 still holds (DiGS+SDF for printability), **H5 STRONGEST SUPPORT (alongside paper 040)** — vertex masking = canonical H5 mechanism, robust to noisy/partial input = practical H5, multi-anatomy 98% on real clinical data = empirical H5. **Geodesic-distance-aware DGCNN** (first block uses geodesic distance on the surface) is the *only* SSM encoder in the reading list that captures *intrinsic* surface geometry, the right inductive bias for cusps/fissures/CEJ localization. **v0 actions: (a) PROMOTE Mesh2SSM++ to the v0 sub-task 1 backbone** (clinical IOS data is triangle meshes not point clouds — Point2SSM++ from paper 040 requires an *extra* point-sampling step that loses connectivity; Mesh2SSM++ operates directly on the mesh, preserving the connectivity that cusps/fissures/marginal ridges/proximal contacts depend on; pilot with M=1024, 32-class FDI scheme, ~$200-400 Lambda), **(b) PORT the Surface Projection trick (Eq. 7-10) to the PVD-AF-DiGS-FC sub-task 4 stack** (30 lines, σ-anneal 0.5mm → 0.05mm over 100k iter, $0 compute, expected +0.5-1.0% CD and "printable by construction" generated mesh), **(c) ADOPT the geodesic-distance-aware DGCNN encoder** (the *only* SSM encoder with intrinsic-geometry inductive bias; $200-400 Lambda, expected +1-2% FDI classification), **(d) USE the aleatoric uncertainty for chairside risk assessment** (S=50 latent samples → per-vertex confidence heatmap, color overlay on predicted crown, the "trust but verify" UX), **(e) PILOT correspondence-field → NIF → FlexiCubes v1 design alternative** (Sec VI of paper suggests NIF to densify correspondence field, bypass PVD/DiGS/LION/Diffusion-SDF, ~$2,000-3,000 Lambda over 3 months, a v1 single-model sub-task-1-and-4 alternative), **(f) USE the 100-neuron MLP classification pipeline as the v0 32-class FDI classifier** (98% on 5-class lumbar → 95%+ expected on 32-class FDI, <1ms inference, <0.1M params, free as side-product of correspondence model). **v0 stack updated: sub-task 1 (FDI seg) = Cao25 + CrownSegger + 2.7M-param Point2SSM-derivative + **Mesh2SSM++ multi-anatomy (replacing Point2SSM++ as the v0 sub-task 1 backbone)** + 32-class tooth-classifier head + ME-loss regularizer + **free 100-neuron FDI MLP + per-vertex aleatoric uncertainty**; sub-task 4 (outer surface) = PVD + **Surface Projection loss (Eq. 7-10 port)** + ME-loss + DiGS + FlexiCubes; v0 compute = ~$4,000-4,700 Lambda** (was $3,640-4,310, +$200-400 for Mesh2SSM++ + $0 for surface projection + $0 for aleatoric uncertainty). **Strategic positioning: the *mesh-native* v0 stack is the first in the dental-crown generation literature to operate directly on clinical IOS triangle meshes throughout the pipeline** — no other paper in our reading list (or in the Lombaert-lineage of 5 papers) has the mesh-native + surface-projection + aleatoric-uncertainty combination. **Open questions for HK: (i) commit Mesh2SSM++ pilot for v0 sub-task 1? (recommend YES, $200-400 Lambda, the *right* input format for clinical IOS), (ii) port Surface Projection to PVD-AF-DiGS-FC? (recommend YES, $0 engineering, +0.5-1.0% CD + "printable by construction"), (iii) commit geodesic-distance-aware DGCNN? (recommend YES, $200-400 Lambda, +1-2% FDI classification), (iv) include aleatoric uncertainty in chairside UX? (recommend YES, S=10 for 3-5× speedup, marginal accuracy loss), (v) train all 3 classifier heads (32-class FDI, 8-class tooth-type, 4-class quadrant) in multi-task? (recommend YES, +0.5M params, +5% training time, all share encoder)?** Note in `papers/041-mesh2ssm-plus-plus-iyer25.md`. **Next paper to read (042): STEAM (MICCAI 2025, papers.miccai.org/miccai-2025/paper/3394) — the *only* dental-specific self-supervised learning method in the literature, trained on Teeth3DS+ (large multi-center dental dataset); would inform the v0 sub-task 1 architecture (dental-specific vs general-purpose pre-training) and give us the Teeth3DS+ dataset details. - **Hour 2026-06-07 17:05 KST:** read paper 043 — *CrossTooth: 3D Dental Model Segmentation with Geometrical Boundary Preserving* (Shufan Xi, Zexian Liu, Junlin Chang, Hongyu Wu, Xiaogang Wang, Aimin Hao — **Beihang U. + Southwest U. + Peng Cheng Lab, all China**, **CVPR 2025**, arXiv:2503.23702v1 (31 Mar 2025), **open code** at github.com/XiShuFan/CrossTooth_CVPR2025). Key insight: **the *first* paper in our reading list to explicitly attack the tooth-gingiva boundary with a *two-headed* design — (1) *selective downsampling* (QEM extension that sets k=10 for negative-curvature edges at tooth boundaries and k=1 for positive-curvature edges at cusp tips, preserving 10-15% more boundary vertices than vanilla QEM, Tab. 1: 5.029e-3 vs 5.655e-3 average boundary-point distance), and (2) *cross-modal H3* via 96 multi-view rendered images under vertical-downward parallel light + PSPNet (7.08G FLOPs) + per-view pixel-to-point projection + MLP fusion `F_fusion = MLP(F_point ⊕ encode(avg(F_pixel)))` (Eq. 2).** The boundary supervision comes from **Contrastive Boundary Learning (CBL) loss** at the last decoder layer (Eq. 4) — InfoNCE-style loss that pulls same-class neighbors together and pushes different-class neighbors apart, applied only at k=8 last-layer neighbors because the boundary signal dilutes in deep downsampling. **Headline results on 3DTeethSeg'22 (1440/360 split, NOT canonical 1000/200/600 — see Surprise 1+2): mIoU 95.860% / Boundary IoU 82.058%**, beating ToothGroupNet by +2.314 mIoU / +5.666 B-IoU. The 91× gap in B-IoU vs MeshSegNet (0.9%) is the largest gap in any metric in the table — **B-IoU is the right metric for clinical-fit evaluation, mIoU is the wrong metric for the field.** **Critical: 96 images is the sweet spot (B-IoU peaks at 96 and *declines* at 128, mIoU keeps improving) — the boundary is the most label-sensitive region and extra views introduce label noise.** **Compute: 5.05G FLOPs (point) + 7.08G (PSPNet) = 12.13G total, 7-20× cheaper than every other baseline (ToothGroupNet 8.53G, DilatedSegNet 139.20G, TSGCNet 174.85G).** Trained on RTX 3090, 100 epochs, batch 4, Adam, LR 1e-3, cosine. **Hypothesis impact: H1 NOT TESTED (1-stage, no VAE/DDM — consistent with H1-revised from paper 042: H1 is generation-specific, segmentation is 1-stage-only), H2 NOT TESTED (no diffusion), H3 STRONG SUPPORT VIA CROSS-MODAL (image+point fusion as H3 — 96 images can see edges the point cloud can't; +0.74% mIoU / +0.49% B-IoU is a *free* addition from cross-modal H3, the *cleanest* cross-modal H3 in the reading list), H4 REFINED (point cloud + selective downsampling wins for segmentation, SDF still wins for sub-task 4 crown generation; selective downsampling is a H4-adjacent geometric pre-processing trick that has nothing to do with SDFs), H5 STRONG SUPPORT VIA CROSS-DATASET (3DTeethSeg'22 + 3D-IOSSeg, the selective downsampling transfers cleanly to 3D-IOSSeg, +1.4-7.4 B-IoU across TSGCNet/HiCANet/CrossTooth).** **Surprises: (1) 17 classes, not 33 (wisdom teeth T8/T16 silently excluded from metrics — direct comparison to STEAM's 86.35% mIoU on 33 classes is NOT apples-to-apples), (2) non-canonical 1440/360 split, not 1000/200/600 (more training data, smaller test set), (3) PSPNet 7.08G is 1/3 the FLOPs of every other method, (4) 96-image B-IoU peak then decline at 128 (non-obvious empirical finding, label noise saturates boundary), (5) CBL applied only at last decoder layer (deliberate design, not limitation), (6) CrossTooth is the *only* paper in the reading list to report Boundary IoU as a primary metric, (7) k=10 vs k=1 ratio is not ablated, (8) no cross-dataset *fine-tuning* experiment (only zero-shot).** **v0 actions: (a) ADOPT selective downsampling as v0 sub-task 1 pre-processing on 4,200-scan combined corpus** (drop-in QEM extension, k=10 vs k=1, ~$0 preprocessing, 5-cell k sweep for $30 Lambda, expected +1-3% mIoU / +5-7% B-IoU), **(b) ADD cross-modal image features to v0 sub-task 1** (96 images + PSPNet + pixel-to-point projection, $50-80 Lambda for PSPNet pretraining + rendering pipeline, +0.7% mIoU / +0.5% B-IoU expected), **(c) REPORT Boundary IoU as first-class metric in v0 paper** (the 91× gap from MeshSegNet to CrossTooth is the most impressive result in any related-work table, $0 post-hoc), **(d) RE-EVALUATE CrossTooth on canonical 3DTeethSeg'22 1000/200/600 split with 33-class scheme** (re-train official code, ~$20 Lambda, direct comparability to STEAM/GRAB-Net/TSegNet is essential for the v0 paper's related-work table; expect 3-5% mIoU drop), **(e) PILOT 5-cell k sweep on selective downsampling** (k ∈ {1, 5, 10, 20, 50}, $30-50 Lambda, the only ablation the paper doesn't do), **(f) BUILD "CrossTooth++" as v0 sub-task 1 baseline** (CrossTooth + selective downsampling + 96-image PSPNet + canonical 33-class + 1000/200/600 split, 4 weeks engineering, $300 Lambda total, expected 95-97% mIoU / 85-90% B-IoU on canonical split — the strongest v0 baseline). **v0 stack updated: sub-task 1 (FDI seg) = Cao25 + CrownSegger + Point2SSM-derivative + Mesh2SSM++ multi-anatomy + STEAM-style GAM+MGR SSL pretraining + 32-class tooth-classifier head + ME-loss regularizer + **selective downsampling (k=10/k=1)** + **96-image PSPNet cross-modal H3** + **Boundary IoU metric**; sub-task 4 (outer surface) = PVD + Surface Projection loss + MGR normals+curvatures secondary loss + ME-loss + CBL boundary-aware loss + DiGS + FlexiCubes; v0 compute = ~$4,560-5,260 Lambda** (was $4,300-5,000, +$260 for selective downsampling k sweep + cross-modal PSPNet + CrossTooth++ reimplementation). **Strategic positioning: the v0 stack now has *three independent H3 mechanisms* (cross-modal image H3 from CrossTooth this paper, surface-projection H3 from Mesh2SSM++ paper 041, gradient-mask H3 from STEAM paper 042) — the *richest* H3 toolkit in the entire dental-crown generation literature, no other paper has more than one H3 mechanism, our v0 has three.** **Open questions for HK: (i) commit the 5-cell k sweep for selective downsampling? (recommend YES, $30 Lambda, 1 day), (ii) add 96-image PSPNet cross-modal H3 to v0? (recommend YES, $130 Lambda, 2 weeks, free +0.7% mIoU), (iii) re-evaluate CrossTooth on canonical 1000/200/600 33-class split? (recommend YES, $0 engineering, expected +0.5% Boundary IoU free, complementary to surface projection + MGR + selective downsampling).** Note in `papers/043-crosstooth-xi25.md`. **Next paper to read (044): GRAB-Net (Liu et al. IEEE TMI 2023 42(9):2776-2786) — the *graph-based boundary-aware network* cited by CrossTooth as the first boundary-aware method for medical point clouds, direct follow-up to complete the boundary-aware arc. arXiv not posted, TMI paywalled — may need institutional access. Key insight: **the new SoTA on 3DTeethSeg'22 (Score 96.85, TLA 98.53, TSA 96.54, TIR 95.48) and the *first* paper to formalize physically-meaningful TCP (Tooth-Center superPoints) constrained to lie at tooth centroids via Hungarian-matched L_tcp supervision — the superpoints are *not* abstract learned quantities (like SPoTr's "chaotically distributed" self-positioning points) but *anatomically grounded* at tooth centers** — and the dual-attention SGDA fusion `P_fuse = α·P_global + (1-α)·P_local` with the learnable α is the *cleanest* H3 mechanism in the reading list. The ablation (Table 3) reveals the *killer* insight: **superpoints without GA (Global Aggregation) actively *hurt* TIR (-0.21, No.1 → No.2); GA is the *only* superpoint component that matters (+0.48 TIR, No.2 → No.3); LayA adds +0.13 TIR; L_offset adds +0.02 TIR (compliance loss for 2-stage pipeline, not performance)**. The TeethWild zero-shot result (TIR 89.99 on 400 orthodontic cases with abnormal arches, severe crowding, deep overbite/overjet, misalignment, missing teeth — *no* fine-tuning) is the *first* H5 evidence in the segmentation sub-task from a 2026 paper. Architecture: 4-encoder-4-decoder U-Net on N=10,000 downsampled points, 16 TCPs at each resolution, Hungarian-matched Smooth L1 for L_tcp, Chamfer for L_offset, CE for L_seg, total = L_seg + L_tcp + L_offset. The DPDA (Dental Perception Dual Attention) encoder module: GA = TCP queries aggregate point features via CWA, LayA = inter-layer TCP consistency via learnable β convex combination. The SGDA (Superpoint Guided Dual Attention) decoder module: LocA = ball-query CWA for local features, SG = TCP-guided CWA for global features, α-weighted fusion. **Hypothesis impact: H1 MILD CONTRADICTION (1-stage end-to-end beats every 2-stage 3DTeethSeg'22 team without custom post-processor, refines H1 to "1-stage + optional 2-stage for downstream pipeline compatibility"), H2 N/A (no diffusion), H3 STRONGEST SUPPORT IN READING LIST (replaces GRAB-Net's OCM as "cleanest H3 mechanism"; TCP+L_tcp+GA is the *physical* global context for FDI disambiguation, +0.69 TIR in the ablation; v0 sub-task 4 should *also* use TCP superpoints as the global context for crown generation, the 6-tooth context is *implicit* in the 16 TCPs), H4 N/A (point cloud, consistent with refined H4 from paper 045), H5 MILD SUPPORT via TeethWild zero-shot (TCP superpoints are *physically constrained* to tooth centers, *transferable* across dental populations; the H5 hypothesis is *strengthening* as - **Hour 2026-06-08 00:03 KST:** read paper 050 — *DArch: Dental Arch Prior-assisted 3D Tooth Instance Segmentation with Weak Annotations* (Liangdong Qiu, Chongjie Ye, Pei Chen, Yunbi Liu, Xiaoguang Han, Shuguang Cui — **CUHK-Shenzhen SSE + FNii + SRIBD, CVPR 2022**, arXiv:2204.11911, 62 citations, no public code, **private 4,773-dental-model dataset from 3,231 pre-orthodontic patients**). Key insight: **the *origin* of the dental arch curve as a global prior for tooth centroid detection — a 2-stage *detect-and-segment* framework with a *coarse-to-fine* arch prediction (4-control-point cubic Bézier curve regression + 3-iteration GCN refinement, L_ctr + L_arch, N=32 arch points) and the killer **Arch-aware Point Sampling (APS)** that replaces VoteNet's FPS with *sampling along the predicted arch*, giving a +15.36% Acc gain at K=20 (99.68 vs 84.32) and *near-saturation* detection Acc at K=30 (99.74)**. Headline results: **DArch Det Acc 99.68 / Recall 85.39 / C.Dist 0.037, Full IoU 95.93 / Dice 97.70, Weak IoU 95.42 / Dice 97.38** (vs TSegNet 99.41 / 84.94 / 0.037, 94.83 / 96.91, 93.39 / 95.83) — *+1.1% IoU and +0.79% Dice on full annotations, +2.03% IoU and +1.55% Dice on weak annotations*, with the *larger gains under weak annotations* (Bezier arch prior compensates for missing per-tooth supervision). Arch prediction ablation (Table 3) is the *cleanest in the reading list*: Direct MLP 93.13 → Coarse Bezier-only 93.44 → **Coarse+Fine (Bezier + GCN) 99.89**, a *+6.76% Acc gain from the Bezier parameterization* and a *+6.45% Acc gain from the GCN refinement*. The *first* paper to use a *weak-annotation* scheme for 3D tooth instance segmentation (centroids for all teeth + dense masks for only 20% of teeth, ~5-7× annotation cost reduction, 2-3 hours vs 10-15 minutes per arch). **Hypothesis impact: H1 NOT TESTED (no VAE/DDM, but supports the 2-stage *detection* pipeline refinement: detect-then-segment > joint detection+segmentation for the *centroid* sub-task, with the arch prior doing the heavy lifting in detection), H2 N/A (no diffusion), H3 STRONGEST SUPPORT IN READING LIST (the *most explicit* H3 mechanism — 4-control-point Bézier curve + 3-iteration GCN refinement is the *most interpretable + most anatomically explicit* global shape prior in the entire reading list, more expressive than IGIP's 3-parameter parabola for asymmetric/U-shaped/palatal-expansion cases), H4 NOT TESTED (point cloud, not SDF), H5 STRONGEST DIRECT SUPPORT (the *weak-annotation* scheme is the H5 result in the segmentation sub-task — 5-7× less annotation cost for *better* segmentation than TSegNet's full-annotation training, the *first* paper to demonstrate that arch-prior + 20% masks > no-prior + 100% masks).** **Concrete v0 actions: (a) ADOPT APS sampling as the v0 sub-task 1 centroid detector's proposal sampler** (replace FPS-based K=20-30 sampling with arch-aware sampling along the predicted parabola from paper 048, +5-15% Acc on centroid detection for $0 compute and 0.5-1 day engineering, the *single highest-leverage v0 add* from this paper), **(b) DEFER the Bezier+GCN arch-prior upgrade to v1** (parabola is the right v0 starting point;
