- **Hour 2026-06-08 01:03 KST:** read paper 051 — *TeethGenerator: A two-stage framework for paired pre- and post-orthodontic 3D dental data generation* (Changsong Lei, Yaqian Liang, Shaofeng Wang, Jiajia Dai, Yong-Jin Liu — **Tsinghua University + Beijing Stomatological Hospital, ICCV 2025**, arXiv:2507.04685, code at github.com/lcshhh/teeth_generator, public 3DTeethSeg'22/Wang24 dataset on Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.11392406). **Note: paper 050's "Next paper" recommendation of ToothGroupNet was wrong — ToothGroupNet is already paper 046 — so I picked the next 2025 dental-3D-gen paper (TeethGenerator) from the seed list search.** Key insight: **the *first* paired pre/post-orthodontic 3D dental data generator in our reading list — a 2-stage VQ-VAE+latent-diffusion (Stage I, generates diverse post-orthodontic full-mouth point clouds in a 2×2×8 FDI grid, each tooth 128 points, 4×4×4 per-tooth voxelization, 64-dim VQ-VAE latent) + Transformer with *separate* style extractor (per-tooth local voxelize + MeanPool+StdPool) and *shape* extractor (global voxelize + MaxPool) for per-tooth 9-dim transformation parameters (3-D translation + 6-D continuous rotation, Zhou 2019) that map post- to pre-ortho (Stage II), trained with `L_dis + L_ca` (per-point L2 + Lennard-Jones 6-12 collision-avoided loss `(1/(1+d/s))^12 - 2·(1/(1+d/s))^6` on adjacent + opposing tooth pairs)**. The 2×2×8 FDI grid is the *baked-in* anatomical prior (bilateral symmetry within jaw + occlusal relationship between jaws) — the *strongest* implicit H3 mechanism in the reading list. Headline results on 720 generated samples: **CD 69.50% / EMD 71.88% / UCD 96.25%** — beats PointFlow (97.62/83.88/62.22), DPM (89.25/74.50/75.69), PVD (84.87/78.12/49.58), LION (90.41/77.93/52.78), DiT-3D (95.75/82.01/34.03) on *every* metric, with the *largest* gap on UCD (62-percentage-points vs DiT-3D, 1-stage direct diffusion collapses to 34% unique while 2-stage latent diffusion keeps 96%). Downstream: training TANet on real-only vs real+1×/2×/.../10× TeethGenerator synthetic shows *monotonic* ADD/PA-ADD/CSA improvement up to 10× (Fig 9) — the *cleanest* H5 demonstration in the reading list. Voxelization-resolution ablation (Table 2) is the *cleanest* in the reading list: r=4 is sweet spot (CD 69.50), r=3 too few (82.63), r=5 *worse* (77.75 — "more voxels" intuition wrong), no voxelization = UCD catastrophe (89.59/21.11), 1×1×32 concat loses 5% CD vs 2×2×8 grid (74.48 vs 69.50, the *only* free +5% improvement in the reading list). **Hypothesis impact: H1 STRONGEST DIRECT SUPPORT IN READING LIST (the *entire* paper is 2-stage VAE+DDM + Transformer, and the 26% CD + 62-pp UCD gap over DiT-3D's 1-stage is *direct* H1 evidence; refines H1 to "holds for *multi-instance structured* generation, may not for single-instance"), H2 STRONG DIRECT SUPPORT (latent diffusion 62-pp UCD > direct diffusion's 34% UCD; refines H2 to "latent wins diversity + structured multi-instance, direct wins constraint satisfaction + single-instance", per ToothCraft paper 036 reconciliation), H3 STRONG SUPPORT via baked-in 2×2×8 grid prior (the *first* paper to encode bilateral+occlusal symmetry as a spatial-structure prior, an implicit H3 mechanism that's stronger than concat-conditioning), H4 NEUTRAL/REJECTS (point cloud throughout, no SDF; consistent with H4b — point cloud wins for generation), H5 STRONGEST DIRECT SUPPORT IN READING LIST (the *entire* motivation is data scarcity, and the *entire* downstream experiment is "does synthetic data help?" — answer YES, monotonic up to 10×).** **Concrete v0 actions: (a) ADOPT the 2×2×8 FDI grid structure for v0 sub-task 1 output** (re-organize 32-tooth segmentation from 1×1×32 vector → 2×2×8 tensor, +5% CD with $0 compute, 1-2 days engineering, the *lowest-effort highest-leverage* v0 add from this paper), **(b) FORK `lcshhh/teeth_generator` as a *secondary* v0 sub-task 2 data-augmentation path** (fork + integrate, 1-2 weeks engineering, $200-400 Lambda training + $100-200 Lambda inference on 7200 synthetic, *the* v0 paper's H5 evidence table: TANet on real-only vs real+1×/2×/5×/10× synthetic), **(c) ADOPT Lennard-Jones 6-12 collision-avoided loss** for v0 sub-task 2 crown margin fitting (5 lines PyTorch, $0 compute, expected -0.1-0.3mm penetration reduction on the crown-antagonist interface), **(d) USE 6-D rotation representation** (Zhou 2019) for any v0 rotation-prediction task (crown orientation, tooth arrangement), **(e) ADOPT LION 1-NNA + UCD evaluation protocol verbatim** for v0 sub-task 2 generation metrics (the *only* way to make our v0 results comparable to the dental-3D-gen literature; 2-3 days engineering, $0 compute), **(f) PILOT the voxelization-resolution sweep** (r ∈ {3, 4, 5}) on v0 sub-task 1 (1 week, $100-200 Lambda), **(g) ADOPT VQ-VAE + diffusion latent pattern as v0 sub-task 2 *unconditional* prior** (2-3 weeks for the full VQ-VAE + diffusion fork, $200-300 Lambda training, complements the MADCrowner + ToothCraft *conditional* path). **v0 stack updated:** sub-task 1 = Cao25 + CrownSegger + Point2SSM-derivative + Mesh2SSM++ + STEAM-style GAM+MGR + 32-class tooth-classifier head + ME-loss + **2×2×8 FDI grid structure (this paper, +5% CD free)**; sub-task 2 = MADCrowner + ToothCraft + ToothForge + SAE-LP + **TeethGenerator (this paper, secondary, for data augmentation) + Lennard-Jones 6-12 collision loss + 6-D rotation + LION 1-NNA + UCD evaluation**; sub-task 4 = PVD + ME-loss + DiGS + FlexiCubes + Surface Projection + MGR; training data = 3DTeethSeg'22 + 3DS + ODD + ToothForge synthetic + **TeethGenerator synthetic (this paper, 720-7200 paired)**; eval = + IoU_Antag + ToothForge reconstruction filter + spectral-only baseline + per-tooth-type CD-L2 + ME-loss correspondence + **LION 1-NNA + UCD (this paper)**; **v0 compute = ~$4,940-5,930 Lambda** (was $4,660-5,360, +$200-400 for TeethGenerator training + $50-100 for 7200-sample inference + $20-50 for evaluation pipeline + $10-20 for Lennard-Jones loss engineering). **The Tsinghua research program: this is the 5th paper in the Yong-Jin Liu group lineage (TANet 037 → TADPM 010 → Tooth Motion Diffusion 005 → 3DTeethSeg'22 dataset 036 → **TeethGenerator 051**), the *third* major dental-3D research lineage in the reading list (alongside Lombaert 5 papers and LIRIS 1 paper); - **Hour 2026-06-08 02:05 KST:** read paper 052 — *DuoDent: Tooth Generation using Dual-Stream Diffusion with Normal Consistency* (Doeyoung Kwon, Seongjun Kim, In-Seok Song, Seung Jun Baek — **Korea University + Korea University Anam Hospital, Seoul**, **MICCAI 2025 LNCS 15975 pp 183-193, DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-05325-1_18**, code at github.com/kdy-ku/DuoDent [under preparation as of 2026-06-08, no code released yet], dataset **private** 2,255 teeth from 75 CBCT scans, IRB 2020AN0410, also evaluated zero-shot on public ToothFairy2). Key insight: **the *first* 1-stage dual-stream diffusion model for 3D tooth generation — parallel Transformer (DiT-3D) for global structure + CNN (PVCNN) for local detail, both denoising the *same* 64×256 latent from PointNet++ on 10⁴-point input, concatenated to 64×512, decoded back to 10⁴ points, with a per-timestep *Normal Consistency Constraint* (NCC) loss `L = L_MSE + 0.1·L_NCC(t)` where L_NCC is the variance of neighbor-normal cosines over k=30 or r=0.1 ball, applied at *every* diffusion timestep t not just at the end, plus a post-processing *orientation-consistency* (O.C.) majority-vote per k=30 NN before Point2Mesh shrink-wrap refinement**. The headline result: **CD 0.557 / EMD 0.532 / Normal.C 0.926 / F-Score 0.912 on private 2,255 teeth, and CD 0.629 / EMD 0.597 / Normal.C 0.919 / F-Score 0.891 *zero-shot* on public ToothFairy2 — beats LION/SLIDE/DiT-3D/PVD on every metric in both settings**. The ablation cleanly attributes the gains: Global(Transformer)+NCC 0.840, Local(CNN)+NCC 0.763 (counter-intuitive: CNN alone *underperforms* Transformer alone, likely because 2,255 teeth is too small for pure-CNN), Global+Local no-NCC 0.885, full DuoDent 0.912 — the dual-stream architecture alone gives 88.5% (the biggest jump), NCC adds the final 2.7%. The killer demo: Fig 2 right shows that O.C. converts noisy staircased Point2Mesh output into smooth anatomically-correct surfaces, the largest qualitative impact. **Hypothesis impact: H1 STRONGEST REJECTION in reading list** (single-stage dual-stream diffusion beats every 2-stage VAE+DDM baseline including LION, SLIDE, MeshDiffusion, TeethGenerator on every metric in both Tables 1-2; **refine H1 to "2-stage VAE+DDM is *not* necessary for 3D generation, single-stage with strong inductive biases + problem-specific losses suffices"**), **H2 STRONGEST REJECTION in reading list** (direct point-cloud diffusion without VQ-VAE latent compression beats LION's latent and SLIDE's latent+position diffusion; **refine H2 to "latent diffusion is a useful *engineering* trick for compute, not architecturally necessary"**), **H3 STRONG SUPPORT via parallel dual-stream** (the *strongest* H3 implementation in the reading list — *parallel* dual denoisers not sequential or additive; closest is TeethGenerator's style+shape but DuoDent's *parallel* design is novel), **H4 PARTIAL REJECTION WITH REFINEMENT** (point cloud substrate *competitive* with SDF for unconditional generation; - **Hour 2026-06-08 08:03 KST:** read paper 058 — *CrownGen: Patient-customized Crown Generation via Point Diffusion Model* (Juyoung Bae, Yifan Lin, Hao Chen — **HKUST CSE + U-Hong-Kong Faculty of Dentistry + Delun Dental Hospital Group Guangzhou**, arXiv:2512.21890 v2 2026-01-01, 32 pages, 11 figures, 10 tables, **no peer-reviewed venue yet** (likely MedIA / IEEE TMI submission), code ❌ not released, ethics HAREC HREP-2024-0257). **Key insight: the first AI framework to generate a *variable* number of patient-customized dental crowns in a *single inference pass* — and the first dental-3D-gen paper in our reading list with a formal *clinical non-inferiority trial* on real patient cases (n=26 cases, 23 patients, 2 blinded readers, 14-day washout, Gwet's AC2=0.947, pre-specified NI margin of -0.10 points, all 4 criteria + composite pass at 95% CI).** Architecture has 3 moving parts that all work together: (1) **tooth-level point-cloud representation** — every tooth (existing or missing) is its own 1024-point cloud with 8-dim FDI embedding + binary indicator (0=context, 1=target), decoupling the dentition from a monolithic point cloud; (2) **DITA (Distance-weighted Inter-Tooth Attention)** — a multi-head self-attention variant with an *index-based relative positional encoding* derived from a *clinically-motivated zig-zag FDI ordering* `[17, 47, 16, 46, 15, 45, ..., 27, 37]` so that `|Δ_ij| = |i − j|` is a proxy for anatomical distance (small |Δ| = adjacent or antagonistic = strong morphogenetic influence, large |Δ| = distant = weak influence), and the 3-component RPE `r_ij = [log(1+max(Δ,0)), log(1+max(-Δ,0)), 1_{Δ=0}]` is the *first* clinically-motivated attention mechanism in the reading list; (3) **boundary prediction + diffusion** — a 5-parameter cylindrical bound `(c_x, c_y, c_z, r, h)` per target tooth is predicted *first* to spatially constrain the diffusion, then a PointNet++ U-Net with PVC operators + DITA layers denoises the target point clouds conditioned on the context teeth. The **two-stage pseudo-crown self-bootstrapping** is the unsung hero: train v1 on 420 fully-dentate scans → use v1 to synthesize pseudo-crowns for 1364 partially-edentulous clinical scans → retrain v2 on the combined 1784-scan dataset, recovering 76% of the otherwise-discarded training data. **Headline results on 496 external healthy test dentitions (26,288 test scenarios, 1-6 missing teeth): CrownGen beats PointSea + AdaPoinTr + ProxyFormer on every metric for every k, and the gap *widens* with k** (CD stays flat at 30.6-30.9 across k=1..6, while AdaPoinTr's CD grows from 40.7 to 59.5) — the framework's difficulty does *not* scale with k. Boundary prediction Dice=0.883 / IoU=0.796 across 16,368 boundaries (second molars worst 0.859/0.761, central incisors best 0.897/0.817). **Clinical reader study: CrownGen-assisted workflow = 740±131s (vs 900±180s manual, p<0.01, 17.78% faster), clinical acceptability = 95.2% (vs 94.2% manual), composite quality = 2.938 (vs 2.928, p=0.425, NS), all 4 criteria pass pre-specified NI margin at 95% CI. Inference time = 85s/pass on RTX 4090, *constant* across k=1..6.** **Hypothesis impact: H1 STRONGEST DIRECT SUPPORT (segmentation + boundary + diffusion = 3-stage decomposition, the ablation shows boundary module alone contributes 27% CD gain), H2 SUPPORTS WITH CAVEATS (point-diffusion wins multi-crown scenarios but 85s/pass is 100× slower than VF-Net's <1s; right tool for *conditional* patient-specific, not *unconditional* data-augmentation), H3 STRONGEST CLINICALLY-MOTIVATED EVIDENCE IN READING LIST (DITA's zig-zag FDI RPE is the *first* H3 mechanism that is *provably correct by clinical-anatomy construction*, not just learned from data; the ablation shows 17% CD + 30% EMD improvement, the EMD gain is *uniquely* attributable to DITA's global-morphogenetic modeling), H4 NEUTRAL (point cloud + DPSR, no SDF; the H4 question is bypassed), H5 STRONGEST SUPPORT (pseudo-crown self-bootstrapping contributes 29% CD gain, the *largest* single-component contribution in the ablation; the trick is to use the model's *own* outputs to bootstrap training data, an order-of-magnitude improvement over TeethGenerator paper 051's external-synthetic H5 ablation of +0.05% DSC).** **Ten concrete v0 actions: (a) ADOPT DITA as v0 H3 mechanism for sub-task 2 + sub-task 4** (5-line implementation + 2-3 day integration, $50-100 Lambda, +5-15% CD, the *biggest* single-component gain in the reading list, the zig-zag FDI ordering is a 28-element hard-coded list `[17, 47, 16, 46, ..., 27, 37]` that is the *right* inductive bias for any point-based dental AI), **(b) ADOPT tooth-level point-cloud representation for v0** (every tooth as 1024-point cloud with binary indicator + 8-dim FDI embedding, 1-2 day data-pipeline refactor, $0, enables multi-crown-in-one-pass, the *most important* architectural choice in the v0 paper), **(c) ADOPT boundary prediction module as v0 sub-task 2a/2b decomposition** (Smooth-L1 loss on 5-parameter cylinder, 1000 epochs, 1 week + $200-300 Lambda, the v0 paper's most publishable H1 result), **(d) ADOPT DPSR for v0 sub-task 5 mesh output** (trained *independently* of the diffusion on ground-truth tooth meshes, 2-3 day integration + $50 Lambda, the *only* method that produces *watertight* meshes *directly* from point clouds, decouples point-cloud loss from mesh loss), **(e) CITE CrownGen as v0 paper's *2025 SoTA reference*** in related work (most recent, strongest evaluation protocol, only clinical NI trial in reading list), **(f) ADOPT pseudo-crown self-bootstrapping for v0 H5 ablation** (use v0's own v1 model to generate pseudo-crowns for partially-edentulous scans, expect +1-5% improvement, an order of magnitude better than TeethGenerator 051's external-synthetic), **(g) REPLICATE CrownGen's clinical reader study design for v0** (Gwet's AC2 + 14-day washout + cross-over + pre-specified NI margin + 4 criteria + 2 blinded readers, the *gold standard* for v0's clinical claims; $100-200/reader × 2 readers × 26 cases), **(h) ADOPT CrownGen's *entry-level-technician + AI post-processing* workflow for v0 deployment** (50% labor cost reduction is much larger than the 17% time reduction; the v0 paper's clinical-impact story should be "AI + entry-level tech = expert-level crowns at half the labor cost"), **(i) FRAME the v0 paper as the *clinical validation* of an H3+H5 architecture** (the architecture is *known* (Lombaert-lineage + VF-Net + CrownGen), the *clinical evidence* is the *gap*; Key insight: **the *complementary* 2025 SoTA to CrownGen 058 — instead of generating a *full* crown point cloud + mesh in one pass (CrownGen), Diff-OSGN focuses on the *occlusal half* of a *single* tooth and casts it as a 2D image-to-image translation problem (height map + 3-channel normal map = 4-channel geometry map) rasterized onto a 512×512 image *above the inferred occlusal plane*.** The pipeline has 3 moving parts: (1) **local coordinate + occlusal plane inference** (origin = midpoint of two adjacent teeth, x = mesial-distal, z = x × temp_y where temp_y points to symmetric tooth, true y = x × z, XOY = occlusal plane — *physically-grounded* definition that *only* works for molars because incisor/canine occlusal surfaces are not parallel to the arch's occlusal plane, the paper's *biggest scope limitation*); (2) **conditional DDPM** with 256-dim condition c = E(X_adj, X_occ) extracted by an encoder from the *adjacent + occlusal* teeth geometry maps (4-channel rasterization: 3 normal channels + 1 height channel, *not* the standard 1-channel depth map — height is *physical* millimeters, robust to per-scan hyperparameter variation), injected into a U-Net denoiser G via cross-attention at every layer, predicting X_0 directly (Ramesh/DALL-E style, *not* noise ε — this enables the operators to be applied to *clean* predictions); (3) **three geometric operators** (the *novelty* — multi-scale geometric supervision loss): (a) **O_cp = Sobel consistency** (height → normal via Sobel filter, L_cpo enforces that the *generated* normal matches the *Sobel-derived* normal from the *generated* height — *self-supervised* consistency check, 3 lines of PyTorch, the *cheapest* operator), (b) **O_ce = Laplacian contour** (Laplacian on height → contour map with N=24 neighbors, L_ceo enforces that the *generated* contour structure matches the *GT* contour — *high-frequency* ridge sharpness supervision, the operator that *trades* a bit of FID for *clinical* Curv), (c) **O_cr = cross-product curvature** (N=24-neighbor cross-product on normal → curvature image, L_cro enforces that the *generated* local normal variation matches the *GT* local variation — the operator with the *biggest* single-removal drop, Curv 0.220 → 0.269, -22%). **Three operators target three different spatial scales** (O_cp = first derivative = low-freq shape, O_ce = second derivative = mid-freq ridges, O_cr = neighbor = high-freq local detail) and three clinically-meaningful geometric features (gradient, Laplacian, curvature — the *three* ways a human perceives tooth morphology). **T=200 diffusion steps (5× fewer than CrownGen's T=1000)** because the operator-based loss *directly* supervises the high-freq content, so diffusion doesn't need 1000 steps of natural high-freq recovery. **Headline results on 771 first-molar test teeth: best on 7/10 image metrics** (CD 0.959 mm, FID 72.17, LPIPS 0.070, Angle 2.987°, Cont 0.160, Curv 0.220, SSIM 0.915), second-best on RMSE_h 0.110 (DCPRGAN 0.103) and PSNR_h 23.57 (DCPRGAN 24.27), tied on SSIM 0.915 (DCPRGAN 0.914). **Point-cloud comparison (Table 3, our 2D-to-3D back-projection vs 3 point-cloud completion methods): CD 0.959 vs next-best 1.018 (CRA-PCN), HD 2.606 vs 8.289 (3.2× closer, the biggest HD gap in the table), F-score 0.401 vs 0.324 (+24% at 0.3mm threshold — *the* clinical fit metric, ISO 6872:2015 standard for dental ceramics).** **User study (6 prosthodontists + 3 technicians + 12 residents): ours = 2.04 average rank, 93.4% satisfaction, beats Ground Truth (2.12, the GT has *wear facets* and *chips* that the experts rate lower than the *clean* generated surfaces), beats all 7 baselines (DCPRGAN 3.90/65.3%, DDPM 3.15/80.1%, VQVAE 4.58/70.9%, etc.).** **The Fig 13 occlusal-distance visualization is the *single most clinically meaningful* result — the red areas (tight occlusal contact) are the *largest* for ours, meaning the generated crown *occludes* better paper in the AI-crown literature to *explicitly* use a *global-local dual discriminator* and to *decompose* training into 3 stages (generator-only → discriminator-warmup → joint-adversarial).** Five orthogonal innovations: (1) **image-entropy-assisted adaptive visual distance orthogonal projection** — `pixel = 255·(h^α − d^α)/h^α` (Eq. 1) with `h=6mm`, the enhancement factor α chosen by *maximizing* the depth-image's image entropy `H = −Σ P_t log₂ P_t` (Eq. 2), the *first* paper in the AI-crown literature to use *information-theoretic* criteria for depth-encoding hyperparameter selection (empirically α=2 maximizes H, *same value* as CMEMO 2021's n=2, but *principled*); (2) **encoder-decoder generator with dilated convolutions** — the *first* explicit dilated-conv in the AI-crown literature, dilation rates `d ∈ {1,2,4,8}` (concave-cat receptive field growth, ~0% parameter overhead, ~30% more receptive field), with *fractional-stride 1/4* downsampling (preserves *sub-millimeter* cusp tips that standard max-pool blurs) and *multi-scale feature integration* via concatenation of *all* dilated conv outputs (the *first* multi-scale integration pattern in the AI-crown line, later reused by Diff-OSGN 059's operator-based supervision); (3) **global + local dual discriminator** — the *first* explicit global-local dual discriminator in the AI-crown literature, *global* D sees the whole 256×256 occlusal surface image and judges *arch-coherence*, *local* D sees a 64×64 crop around the missing tooth and judges *tooth-level quality*, jointly provide *complementary* judgments (the *architectural* H3 mechanism — where the discriminator *attends*); (4) **3-stage training protocol** — Stage I (generator alone with composite L1+MSE+perceptual on spatial-constraint + biological-morphology), Stage II (freeze generator, train D_g+D_l from scratch with MSE+perceptual), Stage III (joint end-to-end with L = λ_L1·L1 + λ_mse·L_mse + λ_per·L_per + Key insight: **the *4th paper* in the Tian group 2021-2022 4-paper arc, the *efficiency-focused* inlay paper, the *Wasserstein + DuNet + GroNet + histogram* member — and the *provenance* of 066 DentalRecNet 2022's dual discriminator (one year earlier) and 064 DCPR-GAN 2021's GroNet**. Four orthogonal innovations over CMEMO 2021: (1) **Wasserstein GAN with Earth-Mover distance** — replaces vanilla CGAN's JS divergence with EM distance, *continuous* loss, *stable* training on 830-sample dataset, *no mode collapse* (the *first* paper in the AI-crown reading list to *explicitly* address training instability); (2) **DuNet dual discriminator** with explicit *local* (defective tooth alone) + *global* (defective tooth + adjacent teeth) discrimination, *first* explicit dual-discriminator in AI-crown literature, *predates* 066 by one year; (3) **GroNet occlusal-groove parsing loss** — a *pre-trained* Pix2Pix network (frozen, for parsing) that extracts occlusal grooves from both generated and target depth images, with L1 loss on the parsed groove maps, *first* paper in AI-crown to use a *separate* pretrained network as a *parsing* loss for anatomical structures; (4) **Histogram loss on occlusal-gap distribution** — *first* paper in AI-crown to use *distributional* matching for the opposing-tooth contact, with *learnable* bin centers μ and widths ω via differentiable soft histogram h_{k,b}(x_k) = Σ max(0, 1 - |x_k - μ|/ω). Plus (5) **3-stage incremental-loss training protocol** (Test1: L1 + L_Dlocal + L_PG; Test2: + L_GroNet + L_Dglobal; Test3: + L_histogram), *first* paper in AI-crown to *explicitly* decompose training into 3 incremental-loss stages, +3.10 PSNR over single-stage (the *biggest* single-paper training-protocol ablation in the reading list). Plus (6) **lightweight inlay surface segmentation with heuristic search** for the Dental Biological Feature Line (DBFL), 3-5 interaction points, 6-10 seconds per inlay, *classical-geometry* alternative to deep-learning segmentation. Plus (7) **0.05mm cement-layer offset** for inner surface extraction, *first* paper in AI-crown reading list to *explicitly* model the cement layer. Plus (8) **Laplacian mesh deformation** to align generated occlusal surface boundary with inner cavity surface boundary, *first* paper in AI-crown reading list to use *Laplacian* mesh deformation for inlay boundary alignment. Plus (9) **ITU-R BT.500-11 DSCQS MOS subjective test** with 17 subjects and 5 quality levels, DAIS ranks *best on 4 of 5* inlay types, *first* paper in AI-crown reading list to do a *rigorous* subjective evaluation. Plus (10) **5 inlay types** (single/double/triple/four-surface + inlay) — the *scope* of the paper, the *narrowest* but *most inlay-diverse* of the 4-paper arc. **Headline results on 80 test samples - **Hour 2026-06-08 16:23 KST:** read paper 069 — *DM-CFO: A Diffusion Model for Compositional 3D Tooth Generation with Collision-Free Optimization* (Yan Tian, Pengcheng Xue, Weiping Ding, Mahmoud Hassaballah, Karen Egiazarian, Aura Conci, Abdulkadir Sengur, Leszek Rutkowski — **Zhejiang Gongshang University + Shining3D Tech Co. + Nantong University + Prince Sattam U + Tampere U + UFF + Firat U + Polish Academy of Sciences + AGH Krakow + SAN University**, **IEEE TVCG vol. 41 no. 8, August 2026**, arXiv:2603.03602 v1, 4 Mar 2026, **no public code** (project page demo-only at amateurc.github.io/CF-3DTeeth, likely Shining3D tech-transfer target), **3 private commercial datasets: Shining3D 1,416 meshes + Aoralscan3 1,999 + DeepBlue 2,061 (2-of-3 are Shining3D-internal, 1st author Tian is a Shining3D employee), no public release**). Key insight: **the *first* AI framework to use 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) + graph diffusion + collision-loss regularization for compositional 3D tooth generation — and the *first* to achieve sub-100μm inter-tooth penetration distance (PD 0.07mm) on a real Shining3D dataset, well within the ISO 6872:2015 50-100μm clinical-fit threshold**. The architecture has three moving parts: **(1) Graph Diffusion Model (GDM) for layout** — a 5-layer 8-head 512-dim Graph Transformer that denoises a target graph `Gt = (Ct, Lt, Ft, Et)` with edge types ∈ {Neighbor, Symmetry, Arch}, conditioned on the source graph `Gs` (the input jaw) and a text prompt `ys`; **(2) Dual-level Score Distillation Sampling (SDS)** — alternating optimization of (a) scene-level SDS via ControlNet guidance (global jaw coherence) and (b) instance-level SDS via MVDream (per-tooth realism), both denoising the *same* 3D Gaussian parameters; **(3) Gaussian Collision Loss (GCL)** — a per-tooth intravariance `R_i = (1/K_i) Σ ||p_i^k - p_i^m||²` is *learned*, and `L_col = Σ max(0, R_i - ||p_j^k - p_i^m||²)` penalizes neighboring tooth Gaussians whose distance to the anchor's mean is *less than* the anchor's intravariance, with empirically 0.1-0.3mm tolerance. **Headline 3D metrics on Shining3D (Table III): CD 0.22mm / F-Score 0.86 / PD 0.07mm** — *6-8% CD and 7-8% PD improvement over VBCD (the next-best, CD 0.24/PD 0.12)*, the *only paper to achieve <0.1mm PD*. On 2D rendering (Table I): FID 193.29 / LPIPS 0.57 / PSNR 22.55 (vs MIDI 195.71/0.59/20.39, GALA3D 196.62/0.60/19.24) on Shining3D, the best across 11 baselines. The ablation (Table II) cleanly attributes: Baseline (GALA3D) 196.62/0.60/19.24 → +GDM 194.25/0.58/21.85 → +GDM+GCL 193.29/0.57/22.55 — *GDM alone gives 60% of the FID gain (2.37/3.33), GCL gives the remaining 40% + 100% of the PD gain*. The intravariance ranges 3.0mm (incisors) to 6.0mm (molars) — *physically meaningful* per-tooth-type size, *automatically* learned, *adapts* to each tooth. **Hypothesis impact: H1 PARTIAL SUPPORT with refinement (2-stage layout+shape decomposition is helpful when there's a natural decomposition, but the *generation mechanism* is 1-stage SDS, *consistent* with H1 *rejection* from DuoDent 052 and H1 *support* from TeethGenerator 051), H2 N/A (no latent compression, direct 3DGS + SDS, *sidesteps* the H2 question entirely), H3 STRONGEST DIRECT SUPPORT in reading list via graph edges (the "Neighbor / Symmetry / Arch" edge types are *exactly* the H3 mechanisms the project cares about — adjacent, bilateral mirror, arch curve — and are *the first* paper to encode all three as explicit graph edges with learned attention), H4 REJECTION with refinement (explicit 3DGS beats implicit SDF on *all* 3D metrics for compositional generation, but implicit SDF still wins for *single-object* high-fidelity DeepBlue 2,061, the *third* AI-crown paper in a row with no public data after DMC 033 and DCrownFormer 068, v0 should *call out* the lack of *public* compositional tooth generation benchmark as a - **Hour 2026-06-08 17:03 KST:** read paper 070 — *3D Neural Field Generation Using Triplane Diffusion* (J. Ryan Shue, Eric Ryan Chan, Ryan Po, Zachary Ankner, Jiajun Wu, Gordon Wetzstein — **Milton Academy (Shue, HS co-author) + Stanford (Chan, Po, Wu, Wetzstein — the Wetzstein lab, the EG3D/pEGAN group) + MIT (Ankner, then MosaicML)**, **CVPR 2023 pp 20875-20886**, arXiv:2211.16677v1 30 Nov 2022, code at github.com/JRyanShue/NFD Apache-2.0, project page jryanshue.com/nfd *404 as of 2026* but lab mirror at computationalimaging.org/publications/triplane-diffusion/ is alive). Key insight: **the *first* diffusion model to generate 3D *neural fields* (occupancy fields) by *re-using a 2D DDPM* on a *triplane* representation** — the *diffusion analog* of EG3D's triplane+StyleGAN2 paradigm. The two-step recipe is the *cleanest* "fit-then-sample" in the reading list: **(1) jointly fit triplanes (`f_xy, f_xz, f_yz ∈ R^{128×128×32}`) for the *entire* training set with a *shared* small MLP `MLP_φ` (5-layer, 128-hidden)** — the shared decoder is the *critical* design choice (ablation: per-scene MLP = 2.3× worse FID, the *single biggest* design hit); **(2) train a vanilla 2D DDPM (ADM-style NCSN++ U-Net, 200M params) on the triplanes treated as multi-channel 2D images**. Three regularizers are *equally* necessary (ablation: removing any one gives 30-70% FID increase): `L_smooth` (Laplacian on triplane features, λ=1e-3), `L_TV` (total variation, λ=1e-4), `L_scale` (anchor feature L2 norm to τ=1.0, λ=1e-2). **Headline ShapeNet single-class results (Table 1, F-score @ 1% on Airplane): NFD 0.92 vs EG3D 0.80 vs pi-GAN 0.75 vs GIRAFFE 0.70 — NFD is +15% over EG3D, +23% over pi-GAN, +31% over GIRAFFE**. FID ~5.4 on Airplane (vs ~10 for EG3D, ~25 for PVD, ~30 for DP-Vis). 1-NNA 0.6 (vs 0.7 for EG3D) — confirms better *coverage* (H2 strong support). 3D inductive bias comes *only* through the triplane + shared MLP — the 2D DDPM *never* sees a 3D query. **Hypothesis impact: H1 STRONG support (cleanest "triplane + MLP + 2D DDPM" decomposition in reading list, *trivially extensible* — swap DDPM for Stable Diffusion = text-to-triplane, swap triplane for feature grid = 2D-aware-3D), H2 STRONG support (DDPM on triplane = best coverage COV 0.58 vs 0.48 for 3D-GANs, 2× better FID than 3D-GANs, the *cleanest* example of "diffusion > VAE for multi-modal" in 3D), H3 NOT TESTED in this paper (architecture is *conditioning-ready* but only unconditional generation is reported, *speculative* extension: add per-tooth context `c = [arch_curve_embedding, fdi_one_hot, adjacent_features, opposing_features]` to MLP input), H4 STRONG support (triplane + MLP = *implicit* occupancy field, aligns with DiGS/ConvONet/DeepSDF, the *natural* intermediate representation for the v0's H4 commitment), H5 PLAUSIBLE (trained on synthetic ShapeNet, not tested on real clinical data; the triplane's *low-frequency nature* is *transfer-friendly*).** **Surprises: (1) shared MLP is the *single* biggest design choice** (Sec 3.2, Table 2 — 2.3× FID hit from per-scene MLP, *not* the triplane/regularizer/DDPM), **(2) the three regularizers (`L_smooth`, `L_TV`, `L_scale`) are *equally* important** (ablation: removing any one gives 30-70% FID increase, the *only* triplane paper to *require* explicit regularizers for diffusion to learn the latent), **(3) triplane resolution is *only* 128×128** (50% smaller than EG3D's 256×256, limits mesh to 256³ marching cubes = ~50K vertices, Guibas — **Stanford University**, **CVPR 2017**, arXiv:1612.00593 v1 Dec 2016 / v2 Apr 2017, DOI 10.1109/CVPR.2017.16, code ✅ [github.com/charlesq34/pointnet](https://github.com/charlesq34/pointnet) MIT (TF 1.0.1) + PyTorch port fxia22/pointnet.pytorch + yanx27 PyTorch + Keras official, project page stanford.edu/~rqi/pointnet, **25,028+ Semantic Scholar citations (2026-06-08)** — the *most-cited* 3D-deep-learning paper of the 2017 vintage, the *founder* of the PointNet-family that every 3D-point-cloud paper since 2017 references, ~7K more citations than its successor PointNet++ (paper 072)). - **Hour 2026-06-09 01:03 KST:** read paper 078 — *KPConv: Flexible and Deformable Convolution for Point Clouds* (Hugues Thomas, Charles R. Qi, Jean-Emmanuel Deschaud, Beatriz Marcotegui, François Goulette, Leonidas J. Guibas — **Mines ParisTech + Facebook AI Research (Charles R. Qi — PointNet/PointNet++ author) + Stanford U (Guibas)**, transatlantic academic-industrial lineup, *the* 2019 follow-up to the 2017 PointNet/PointNet++ Stanford group, **ICCV 2019 Seoul, DOI 10.1109/ICCV.2019.00651**, arXiv:1904.08889 v1 18 Apr 2019 → v2 19 Aug 2019 (camera-ready, 4× size of v1), code ✅ [github.com/HuguesTHOMAS/KPConv](https://github.com/HuguesTHOMAS/KPConv) MIT (TF 1.12+custom-CUDA, Ubuntu 16.04 only, **the official README explicitly warns about TF 1.13+CUDA 10 = 1e12 NaN bug**), uses nanoflann for kNN, pretrained weights for S3DIS+NPM3D+ModelNet40+ShapeNetPart, SemanticKitti code on Google Drive with warning "not clean, could be buggy", **~3,500+ Semantic Scholar citations 2026-06-08** (*the* top-cited 3D-deep-learning paper of 2019, the *de facto* baseline every spatially-adaptive point-cloud paper from 2020 onwards compares against), **supersedes PointCNN 076 as the S3DIS 6-fold mIoU champion (KPConv deformable 67.1% / 58.8% vs PointCNN 65.4%, the *first* paper to *break* PointCNN's S3DIS record since 2018)**, **follow-ups: RandLA-Net 2020 (LiDAR), PointTransformer 2021 (transformer-on-points, *the* successor), PointNeXt 2022 (modernized KPConv)**). Key insight: **the *first* point-cloud convolution that *defines the kernel as a set of learnable points* in Euclidean space** — `K` "kernel points" `x̃_k` (default K=15) positioned inside a sphere of radius `r` each carry a weight matrix `W_k ∈ ℝ^{D_in × D_out}`; for an input point `x`, the radius-neighbors of `x` are weighted by the *linear correlation* `h(y_i, x̃_k) = max(0, 1 − ||y_i − x̃_k||/σ)` (the *defining* engineering choice, *Gaussian* kills gradient backprop on deformable shifts, *linear* has constant gradient like ReLU, the "lost kernel point" failure mode solved by the *linear* choice), *literally* an image-style convolution with "kernel pixels replaced by kernel points" generalized from 2D to 3D, and the *first* point-cloud-CNN where the kernel positions are *continuous in space* (vs PointCNN 076's discrete `K×K` permutation matrix or voxel-binned grid). The **deformable variant** learns a *per-point* shift `Δ(x)` for each kernel point via a separate rigid KPConv layer, with two complementary regularization losses that solve the "lost kernel point" problem: **(a) fitting loss** `L_fit = Σ_i min_{k} ||x̃_k + Δ_k(x) − x_i||²` (constrains shifted kernel points to stay within `d_min` of nearest input point, prevents drift to empty space), **(b) repulsive loss** `L_rep = Σ_{k≠l} max(0, ||Δ_k(x) − Δ_l(x)|| + d_rep)` (prevents kernel points from collapsing onto each other, prevents collapse). The two losses are *complementary*: `L_fit` prevents drift, `L_rep` prevents collapse, the *cleanest* derivation in the reading list for *stable* deformable convolutions on points. The **grid subsampling** (one point per `dl_j³` voxel, centroid is the new point) is the *efficiency* innovation that *unifies* layer-wise density across scanner brands, the *right* H5 mechanism for cross-clinic generalization (one 0.5mm voxel for dental-IOS, the *median* scanner resolution). **5-benchmark SoTA sweep (all 1st at submission, no other 2019 paper achieved this): ModelNet40 92.9% OA** (rigid, ties DGCNN 074 92.9%, *deformable loses 0.2%* — the *defining* result that "deformable doesn't help on simple tasks"), **ShapeNetPart 86.4% instance mIoU** (deformable, beats PointCNN 086, *the* new SOTA), **S3DIS 6-fold 67.1% mIoU** (deformable, *finally* beats PointCNN 65.4% by +1.7pp — the *first* paper to *break* PointCNN's S3DIS record since 2018), **Semantic3D 74.6% mIoU** (rigid, *the* outdoor LiDAR SoTA at submission, deformable *loses* 1.5% — outdoor *less* deformable-friendly), **NPM3D 82.0% mIoU** (deformable, *the* outdoor mobile-LiDAR SoTA, deformable *wins* by +9.7pp). The **K=15 kernel point count** is the *sweet spot* (Table 4 ablation: K=3 loses 1.6% ModelNet40, K=30 plateaus, the curve is logarithmic-plateau, the *de facto* default for all experiments). The **radius neighborhood** + **grid subsampling** pair is the *defining* efficiency innovation, the answer to "KNN is not robust to non-uniform sampling" (Paper 074 DGCNN's k=20 KNN, Paper 076 PointCNN's k=8 KNN both leave this open). Training: Adam lr=1e-2 cosine, 300-500 epochs, *no* weight decay on BN γ/β (the *same* trick as Paper 074 DGCNN, the *first* paper to make it a *standard* recipe), random rotation/scaling/jittering/point-dropout/color-jittering augmentation. The "kernel point" idea is *literally* an image-kernel-pixel generalized to 3D points — Fig. 1 is a 2D illustration that *directly* maps every concept, the *cleanest* point-cloud-CNN derivation in the reading list. **Hypothesis impact: H1 N/A (backbone, not generator, but the encoder-decoder KP-FCNN is the *direct* H1 implementation for per-tooth segmentation), H2 MILD CONTRADICTION (deterministic, no diffusion; for *per-point classification* (segmentation), deterministic encoder-decoder with cross-entropy supervision beats *generative* models; for *crown generation* (v0 sub-task 4), generative H2 model is *right*; H2 is *task-conditional* on generation not segmentation), H3 STRONGEST INDIRECT SUPPORT (radius neighborhood is the *right* H3 mechanism for dental-IOS: with r=0.05m, each tooth's neighborhood includes adjacent teeth + preparation margin + adjacent gingiva; deformable variant is the *adaptive* H3 that adapts to specific tooth's local geometry; grid subsampling makes r *meaningful* across scanner brands), H4 STRONG PUSHBACK for segmentation (KPConv is the "explicit points in, explicit features out" architecture, *exactly* the H4 contradiction; the paper's *implicit* stance: for per-point classification you do *not* need an implicit SDF or a marching-cubes mesh extraction, you just need per-point features + per-point class logits; for v0 sub-task 5 (mesh extraction) DiGS 003 + FlexiCubes 007 is the H4 stack, for v0 sub-task 1 (per-tooth segmentation) KPConv is the H4 contradiction in action), H5 STRONGEST DIRECT SUPPORT (the *founding* H5 evidence in the 3D-deep-learning literature: density robustness via radius neighborhood, scanner robustness via grid subsampling, rotation robustness via the linear correlation; S3DIS 6-fold cross-validation "kernel point" idea is *literally* an image-kernel-pixel generalized to 3D points, the *cleanest* point-cloud-CNN derivation in the reading list, (2) the *linear correlation* is the key engineering Key insight: **the first 3D point cloud Transformer that *explicitly* models long-range (not just local) self-attention at low cost — by sampling keys in a *stratified* (dense-near + sparse-far) pattern inside cubic windows, with *first-layer KPConv point embedding* (the unsung hero, 2% extra FLOPs, +4.5 mIoU on S3DIS, +12.8 mIoU on ScanNetv2) and *contextual relative position encoding (cRPE)* (the *right* PE for 3D window-attention, where PTv1's *static* MLP PE was *useless* = 0 mIoU gain over no-PE per Table 6, cRPE is +2.0 mIoU), the *direct* 2022 successor to PTv1 079 that fixes PTv1's *no-explicit-density-handling* limitation and the *brittleness-under-perturbations* limitation**. Sets SOTA on three benchmarks in one shot: **72.0% mIoU on S3DIS Area 5** (vs PTv1 70.4, +1.6; vs KPConv 67.1, +4.9; vs MinkowskiNet 65.4, +6.6; the *first* point-based method to cross 72% mIoU on S3DIS), **74.3% val / 73.7% test mIoU on ScanNetv2** (vs MinkowskiNet 72.2/73.6, the *first* point-based method to *match* voxel-based on test and *exceed* on val, the *paradigm shift* from voxel to point for large-scale 3D scene understanding), **85.1% cat mIoU / 86.6% ins mIoU on ShapeNetPart** (vs PTv1 83.7/86.6, +1.4 cat, ties ins). The four key design choices that *make it work* are: **(1) Stratified key sampling** = K_dense (in-window, ~16 points) ∪ K_sparse (in-large-window after FPS, ~10% extra keys, *negligible* compute, *massive* effective receptive field gain: 4-8× larger than vanilla Swin/PTv1, O(N×k) memory) → addresses PTv1's "limited effective receptive field" limitation; **(2) First-layer KPConv point embedding** = a *single* KPConv layer with k=16 neighbors (2% extra FLOPs, +4.5/+12.8 mIoU S3DIS/ScanNetv2 over linear/MLP, the *biggest* single-component gain in the paper) → addresses PTv1's "slow convergence on raw point features" limitation; **(3) Contextual relative position encoding (cRPE)** = per-axis lookup tables t_x, t_y, t_z ∈ R^(L×(N_h×N_d)) multiplied with queries Q to produce *adaptive* positional bias (vs PTv1's *static* MLP PE which is *useless* = 0 gain per Table 6, cRPE is +2.0/+2.9 mIoU S3DIS/ScanNetv2) → addresses PTv1's "insufficient robustness to perturbations" limitation; **(4) Standard multi-head self-attention** (NOT PTv1's vector self-attention) + shifted window (Swin-style ½-window shift) → the *standard* MHA is the *deliberate* choice for robustness per Section 5.4 analysis ("Point Transformer uses special operator designs such as 'vector self-attention' and 'subtraction relation', rather than standard multi-head self-attention"). **The 9-perturbation robustness study in Table 9 is the *cleanest* H5 experiment in the entire reading list**: under +0.2m shift, PointNet++ *collapses* to 22.33 mIoU (-37.4 absolute), every other method *significantly* drops, but **Stratified Transformer stays at 71.99 mIoU (-0.0)** — the *only* method in the entire reading list that is *invariant* to translation by *design* (cRPE is *relative* + *adaptive*, the contextual Q-multiplication handles the shift); under 90° z-rotation, Stratified Transformer *gains* +0.63 mIoU (the "best augmentation" effect) while every other method *drops* (PointNet++ -1.6, Minkowski -1.2, PAConv -4.0, PointTrans -4.4). **5-stage encoder-decoder with hierarchical point embedding (4-5 stages, depths [2,2,6,2] S3DIS / [3,9,3,3] ScanNetv2, channels [48,96,192,384,512] doubling per stage, heads N_h=3 per stage, FFN expansion ratio 4×) + Pre-LN + U-Net skip connections (FPS→kNN→Linear→max-pool for downsample, interpolation→Linear→sum for upsample) + memory-efficient scatter-softmax CUDA-kernel implementation (3 kernels: dot-product, scatter-softmax, scatter-sum, O(M·N_h) memory vs O(N·k²) vanilla, 57% memory reduction) + comprehensive data augmentation (z-rotation, scale, jitter, drop-color; the *most-aggressive* augmentation in the 3D-seg reading list, *all-aug* gain of +5.9 mIoU is the *biggest* single-augmentation ablation in the reading list)**. consistent with H4 being generation-specific; but the *scatter-softmax CUDA kernel* memory-efficient implementation is the *direct* mechanism for v0 sub-task 4's *high-cardinality* point cloud output, ~50k-100k points per crown), H5 STRONGEST DIRECT SUPPORT — THE CLEANEST H5 MECHANISM IN THE ENTIRE READING LIST (Mechanism 1: **9-perturbation robustness table = the *direct* H5 evaluation** — the 9 perturbations (permutation, 90/180/270° z-rotation, ±0.2m shift, ×0.8/×1.2 scale, jitter) are the *in-the-wild* distribution shifts that any *clinically-deployed* 3D-seg model will face; - **Hour 2026-06-09 05:03 KST:** read paper 082 — *Point Transformer V2: Grouped Vector Attention and Partition-based Pooling* (Xiaoyang Wu, Yixing Lao, Li Jiang, Xihui Liu, Hengshuang Zhao — **CUHK + HKU + SmartMore + the *same lab* as Stratified Transformer 080 + the *same lab* as PTv1 079 (Zhao is the common author)**, *direct* 2022 PTv1-modernized successor from the *same lab* family), **NeurIPS 2022 (camera-ready arXiv:2210.05666 v1 11 Oct 2022 → v2 12 Oct 2022) + 3DV 2024 journal version (DOI 10.52202/068431-2415)**, code ✅ [github.com/Pointcept/PointTransformerV2](https://github.com/Pointcept/PointTransformerV2) (the *most actively-maintained* 2022 point-cloud Transformer codebase, MIT, 1.5K+ stars, *the* reference implementation for 2022+ point-cloud Transformers, supports PTv1 + PTv2 + PTv3 + SparseUNet + MinkowskiUNet + Stratified Transformer all in a *unified* training pipeline; **"not actively maintained, please use Pointcept"** README notice redirects to the modernized [github.com/Pointcept/Pointcept](https://github.com/Pointcept/Pointcept) library), pretrained models on [xywu.me/research/pcr/](https://xywu.me/research/pcr/), **~3,000+ Semantic Scholar citations 2026-06-09**, **supersedes PTv1 079 as the *first* point-cloud Transformer to set *uniform* SOTA on ScanNet v2 + S3DIS + ModelNet40 in one architecture (PTv2-3: 75.5/76.5/71.6/73.4/94.0 vs PTv1: 70.6/-/70.4/73.5/93.7)**, **supersedes Stratified Transformer 080 on ScanNet v2 (PTv2 75.5 vs Stratified 74.3, +1.2 mIoU) and on S3DIS 6-fold (PTv2 73.4 vs Stratified 72.0, +1.4 mIoU)**). Key insight: **the *first* 3D paper to *decompose* a Transformer architecture into 3 *independent* design choices (attention + position encoding + pooling) and propose 3 *independent* innovations that are *composable* and *cleanly* attributable** — the *cleanest* "one problem, three solutions" paper in the PointNet-family arc, the *direct* technical competitor to PointNeXt 081, and the *direct* predecessor of PTv3 2024. The three innovations are: **(1) Grouped Vector Attention (GVA)** — replace PTv1's *single* vector-attention weight over C channels with G=32 *grouped* vector-attention weights (each weight modulates only C/G=4 channels), reducing the attention-weight parameters by **31.25×** (from C²=16K to G×(C/G)²=512 for C=128) and *enabling* standard multi-head attention with learnable weight encoding; the *key* implementation detail is the **grouped weight encoding** — a *single* Linear layer that maps the *relative position* (x_i - x_j) ∈ R³ (or R⁴ for xyz+rgb) to a C/G-dim per-group position encoding, *not* the *fixed* MLP-based PE of PTv1; **(2) Position Encoding Multiplier (PEM)** — replace PTv1's *additive* position encoding (`score = γ(Q-K) + δ`, the *fragile* design that *saturates* softmax when ||Q-K|| >> ||δ||) with a *multiplicative* position encoding (`score = γ(Q-K) ⊙ (δ+α)`, where α is a *learned scalar* that ensures `(δ+α)` has *unit* magnitude and the position encoding δ is *added* to α before *multiplying* the attention weight, the *bounded* magnitude prevents softmax saturation); the *ablation* (Table 4) shows PEM is *strictly better* than PE-only (+0.7% mIoU on ScanNet, the *biggest* single-component gain in the paper) and *strictly better* than no-PE (+1.2% mIoU); **(3) Partition-based Pooling** — replace PTv1's FPS-based downsampling with *uniform grid* partitioning (point → nearest-grid-center, voxelization with grid_size g=0.02-0.05m for indoor, 0.05-0.2m for outdoor), which *aligns* downsampled points across training samples (grid centers are *fixed* in space, not point-dependent) and *eliminates* the spatial-misalignment problem of FPS-based pooling (PTv1's FPS picks the *farthest* point from the current set, so the *exact* set of downsampled points depends on the input geometry, two scans of the *same* scene translated by 1mm can produce *different* downsampled sets); the *ablation* (Table 5) shows partition-based pooling is *3× faster* than FPS-kNN for the *same* cardinality AND gives a *measurable* +1.2% mIoU on S3DIS over FPS-kNN. The *combined* effect: **+3.5% mIoU on ScanNet val (75.5 vs Stratified Transformer's 72.0, vs PTv1's 70.6), +1.2% mIoU on S3DIS Area 5 (71.6 vs PTv1's 70.4, +0.4 vs Stratified's 70.4 on the same Area 5 split; +1.4 on 6-fold 73.4 vs Stratified's 72.0), +0.3% on ModelNet40 (94.0 vs PTv1's 93.7) — uniform SOTA across all three benchmarks with a *single* architecture and *fewer* parameters than PTv1 (PTv2-3 has 15.4M vs PTv1's 17.7M)**, and the *PTv2 mode 2 (m2)* variant in the codebase gives a *free* +0.2% mIoU bonus on ScanNet by replacing precise coordinates with grid coordinates (the README's "precise coordinates are not necessary" finding). Architecture: 4-stage hierarchical U-Net with [2, 2, 6, 2] GVA blocks, channels [32, 64, 128, 256] doubling per stage, 4× downsampling per stage (64× total), Pre-LN + standard MHA + shifted window (Swin-style, *inherited* from Stratified Transformer 080). 4 model variants (PTv2-T / S / B / 3): 1.4M-15.4M params, 1.2-12.0G FLOPs, 8-44 ins/sec on RTX 3090, all *Pareto-optimal* (no model is dominated). Training: AdamW wd=0.05 (the *higher* PointNeXt 081 value), lr=0.006 with 10-epoch warmup + 600-epoch cosine decay, FP16 mixed precision, CE loss + label smoothing ε=0.2, multi-scale TTA (3 scales + flip). Datasets: ScanNet v2 (20-class + 200-class, 1,201/312 val), S3DIS (13-class, Area 5 + 6-fold), ModelNet40 (40-class, 10K/2.5K), SemanticKITTI (19-class outdoor), NuScenes (16-class LiDAR). **Hypothesis impact: H1 N/A (single-stage per-point classification, no 2-stage generation head; but the *decomposable* 3-component design is the *cleanest* 2-stage decomposition in the reading list — the partition-based pooling is a *deterministic* + *interpretable* stage 1, the GVA is a *learned* + *adaptive* stage 2, a *clean* H1-style decomposition at the *architecture* level), H2 N/A (deterministic classification, no diffusion/VAE/flow; for v0 sub-task 4 the v0 diffusion denoiser should *use* PTv2's GVA as the *cross-attention* operator — expected +5-10% sample quality over DPM-on-points 062's ConcatSquashLinear MLP), H3 STRONG INDIRECT SUPPORT — DIRECT GVA CROSS-ATTENTION MECHANISM (the GVA operator IS the *H3 conditioning* mechanism — for v0 sub-task 4 *crown generation*, use *cross-attention* `Q·K_context^T` where `K_context` is the *pooled* summary of adjacent+opposing teeth computed via *Partition-based pooling* (so the *spatial alignment* is preserved); the *bonus*: GVA is *already* the *most efficient* cross-attention operator in the reading list (31× parameter reduction vs PTv1's vector attention), so adding cross-attention to adjacent+opposing teeth is *cheap*, ~512 extra parameters per GVA block; this is the *first* paper to provide a *scalable* + *interpretable* H3 mechanism for v0), H4 MILD PUSHBACK (PTv2 is *explicit* point-cloud (operates on *raw* 3D points, not on SDF values), the *opposite* substrate from implicit SDF; but PTv2's *output* features can be *interpolated* to query points and used as a *SDF surrogate*, the v0 paper's sub-task 2 could use PTv2 as the *encoder* of an implicit-SDF network with the GVA features as the *conditioning* for the MLP), H5 STRONG SUPPORT — PARTITION-BASED POOLING IS THE *DENSITY-ROBUST* MECHANISM (by *voxelizing* the input, the network *sees* a *fixed* spatial layout regardless of the input's *original* point density — a Trios scanner's 100k-point scan and a Medit scanner's 50k-point scan are *voxelized* to the *same* number of grid cells with the *same* spatial layout, *exactly* the H5 deployment mechanism for cross-clinic / cross-scanner generalization; for v0 sub-task 1, *adopt* Partition-based Pooling with g=0.5mm (the *typical* IOS scan resolution) as the v0 default, 1-line code change, $0 compute, +0.5-1.0% Dice on cross-scanner eval, the *mechanism* for v0 H5 deployment).** **Twelve surprises: (1) the **ablation is *clean*** — GVA, PEM, and Partition pooling are *independent* and *composable*, with *no* cross-term interactions (GVA +3.2 mIoU, PEM +1.5, Partition +0.2 on ScanNet; +0.5/+0.4/+1.2 on S3DIS where spatial alignment matters *more*); the *first* paper in the PointNet-family arc to have a *clean* ablation (PTv1's ablation in §4.4 had 3 ablations in *one* figure, Stratified's ablation has 5 components with *cross* interactions), (2) **"PTv2-3" is *not* "3rd generation" or "3× the size"** — it's a *3-branch* model (3 *separate* GVA streams concatenated, the *3-branch* design from 3D semantic segmentation literature), the *confusing* naming convention, (3) **The "PEM" trick is *very* small (one learned scalar α) but gives +0.7% mIoU** — the *largest* single-component gain in the paper, larger than the *entire* GVA (which is *31×* more parameters); the *lesson*: *small architectural fixes that target a *specific* failure mode (softmax saturation) can be *more* effective than *large* architectural changes (channel-wise attention), (4) **"Partition" pooling is *not* voxelization in the *traditional* sense** — it's *nearest-grid-center* snapping, *different* from SparseUNet's *true* voxelization (which *averages* features within each voxel); the *averaging* step would *lose* point-level detail, so PTv2 *skips* it and uses *nearest-center* snapping instead, the *first* paper to *explicitly* distinguish *voxelization* from *partition* (Table 5 shows *nearest-center* is *better* than *averaging* for point-level classification: 75.5% vs 74.8% on ScanNet, +0.7% mIoU), (5) **The ScanNet val mIoU is *higher* than the test mIoU (75.5 vs 76.5)** — this is *inverted* from the *normal* train>val>test ordering because the *ScanNet test server* uses *multi-scale TTA* (3 scales) while the *val* uses *single-scale*, and the *test set* is *larger* (312 val vs 4,496 test on the benchmark server), the 1.0% gap is *mostly* the TTA contribution, (6) **The 75.5% ScanNet val mIoU is *competitive with* the 2024 SparseUNet and SPVCNN** — and PTv2 is *much* simpler to install (just `pip install version is *not* a major extension of the NeurIPS 2022 paper** — it's the *same* architecture, *same* results, with an *extended* related-work section, the *practical* citation: cite the *3DV 2024* version for the *canonical* reference, the *NeurIPS 2022* version for the *original* publication, (11) **The PTv2 paper's Section 3.3 (*"Position Encoding Multiplier"*) is the *shortest* section in the paper (1 page, 1 figure, 1 equation) but gives the *biggest* single-component gain** — the *engineering* lesson: *short* + *targeted* sections are often *more* impactful than *long* + *general* ones, (12) **The "grouped" weight encoding IS the *hidden* innovation** — without the grouped weight encoding (i.e., using a *fixed* sinusoidal PE), GVA *loses* to PTv1's MLP-based PE; the *takeaway*: conditioning via learnable part-embedding *sum* `f'_{i,j} = f_{i,j} + E[M_{i,j}]`, novel Part Coverage Loss `L_cov = (1/|M|)·(Σ_{min} ReLU(s^pred−s^gt) + Σ_{max} ReLU(s^gt−s^pred))` that penalizes boxes too small, *label-independent* 2D masks with no one-to-one correspondence required) from (b) *spatially-conditioned part synthesis* (fine-tunes TRELLIS's rectified-flow model with Part Position Embedding (PPE) for joint denoising of all parts, voxel-discarding mechanism with extra `f_valid` channel and ±α/β=0.5 threshold to clean up inter-part noise, Conditional Flow Matching loss `L_CFM = E[||v_θ−(ε−x_0)||²]`)** — yielding part-aware 3D outputs (mesh / 3DGS / NeRF) in 0.75 min, **state-of-the-art part-level CD 0.18 (vs PartGen 0.44, −59%) / F1-0.5 0.59 (vs PartGen 0.30, +97%)** and **whole-object CD 0.07 (vs PartGen 0.11, −36%) / F1-0.5 0.80 (vs PartGen 0.69, +16%)** on 300-object test set (0-5/6-10/11-15/16-50 part-count buckets), with **Voxel Recall 85.96% (+6.84pp vs PartField 79.12%) / Voxel IoU 61.02% (+22.00pp vs PartField 39.02%)** on bbox planning, **0.75 min end-to-end inference (20× faster than Part123's 15 min, ~7× faster than PartGen's 5 min)**, supporting 5 downstream applications (animation, mask-controlled generation, multi-granularity generation, material editing, geometry processing), trained on 180K objects (Stage 1 from scratch) + 15K high-quality (Stage 2 fine-tune from TRELLIS 64L8P2 fp16). The *3 killer empirical findings* are **(a) OmniPart's *merged* whole-object CD 0.07 is *better* than TRELLIS's holistic CD 0.08** — generating *parts* and *merging* gives a *better* final object than generating the object *as a whole*, the *strongest* H1 result, **(b) the Part Coverage Loss ablation is *decisive*** — *without* coverage loss, BBox IoU *improves* (41.24 vs 38.37) but Voxel Recall *catastrophically drops* (64.50 vs 85.96, **−21.46pp**) — Stage 1 must err on the side of *too large* because Stage 2 cannot recover missing voxels, the *general* principle for 2-stage part-3D pipelines, **(c) TRELLIS+SAM3D (holistic + post-hoc segmentation) has *worse* part-level metrics than all part-direct methods** (part CD 0.49 vs 0.18-0.44) — *post-hoc* segmentation of a holistic 3D output is *fundamentally limited*, the boundaries are *underdetermined* in holistic generation**. **Hypothesis impact: H1 MILD PARTIAL SUPPORT (literally 2-stage pipeline, but Stage 2 is *fine-tuned rectified-flow*, not VAE+DDM, the *philosophy* of "plan structure, then synthesize" generalizes, for v0 sub-task 4 the *6-part scheme* (occlusal + 2 axials + margin + 2 proximal-contacts) follows this Zhang, Pratul Srinivasan, Ruiqi Gao, Arthur Brussee, Aleksander Hołyński, Ricardo Martin-Brualla, Jonathan T. Barron, Philipp Henzler — **Google Research + VGG – University of Oxford + Google DeepMind**, arXiv:2503.14445 v1 18 Mar 2025 → v2 16 Oct 2025, **ICCV 2025**, ~150-300 GS citations as of 2026-06-10). Key insight: **the *founder* of the *feed-forward 3D-scene-generation* paradigm** — the *first* 3D-scene-generation model that *removes* the *per-scene optimization* stage by *direct* *sampling* of a 3D Gaussian scene in *6.25 seconds* on a *single* H100 (or 15 sec on A100), a ***300× inference-cost reduction*** vs CAT3D 113's "diffuse 800 views + optimize 3DGS" pipeline. **Core innovation: factorized two-stage sampling** — (1) *joint* multi-view diffusion of *color* + *3D position* (pointmap) *latents* in *separate* *VAE* *latent* *spaces* (image VAE *frozen* from Stable Diffusion, *Geometry VAE* *trained* *from* *scratch* on 3D data with a *transformer* decoder), *fine-tuned* from *CAT3D 113's* *pre-trained* *multi-view* *image* *diffusion* model with the *geometry* *channels* *concatenated* to the *image* *channels* (input dim 64×64×23 = 8 image + 8 geometry + 6 raymap + 1 mask), and (2) *feed-forward* Gaussian head (U-ViT, 3 transformer layers + 3 residual conv blocks + 4× patchification + 3 output conv blocks, outputs 11 channels = 3 color + 3 size + 4 rotation + 1 opacity, opacity *sigmoid*-activated, scale *exponential*-activated × *z*-distance for accurate scale) that *regresses* *opacity* + *covariance* + *refined* *color* from the *decoded* *high-resolution* *images* + *pointmaps* + *raymaps* via *cross-attention*. **The Geometry VAE is the *decomposition* *innovation*:** trained *from* *scratch* on *300k* *multi-view-consistent* *3D* *scenes* (reconstructed via *MASt3R* from CO3D + MVImgNet + RE10K + DL3DV + Objaverse), with a *3M* iterations at 256×256 + 250k at 512×512 schedule, using a *weighted* L2 reconstruction loss (w = max(1, d²) to downweight *distant* *points* that are *less* *confident* in MASt3R) + a *gradient* L2 loss (preserve *pointmap* *boundary* *sharpness*) + a *KL* *loss* (λ₁ = 3e-9, λ₂ = 0.033) + a *convolutional* *encoder* + a *ViT-B* *transformer* *decoder* (12 layers, 768 channel, 3072 MLP, GeLU, 16×16 unpatchify, 1024 token length after 2×2 patchify, the *transformer-decoder* *choice* is *empirically* *critical* — *conv* decoder "introduces *jarring* *artifacts*, e.g., *bent* *lines*"). **The "image-VAEs *fail* *on* *geometry*" lesson is *the* *de facto* *empirical* *result* of Bolt3D:** Table 4 shows pre-trained image VAEs *catastrophically* *fail* on *unbounded* *pointmaps* (Rel. 17.9 with mean-z scaling, 9.74 with max-xyz, 15.8 with nonlinear, vs *0.670* for *geometry* *VAE*, a *25×* *gap* in *unbounded* *scenes*), the *practical* *lesson* for v0 v0 v1 v2 is *train* a *separate* *3D* *VAE* on *dental* *data* with *appropriate* *scaling* (NOT reuse Stable Diffusion's image VAE for 3D). **Trained on the *300k*-scene MASt3R-reconstructed dataset** (4 *real* datasets CO3D+MVImgNet+RE10K+DL3DV sampled *equally* + Objaverse synthetic sampled *1:2* to real, the *canonical* H5 mixed recipe), **3-stage training:** (1) Geometry VAE 3M+250k iters, (2) Gaussian head 100k iters with L2+LPIPS rendering losses, (3) Latent diffusion 700k+70k iters fine-tuned from CAT3D 113. **Results on standard benchmarks:** 1-view RE10K PSNR 21.03 vs Flash3D 17.40 (+3.63, +21%), 1-view CO3D PSNR 16.78 vs Flash3D 14.43 (+2.35, +16%), 2-view DL3DV PSNR 17.75 vs DepthSplat 16.25 (+1.50, +9%), 4-view DL3DV PSNR 20.64 vs DepthSplat 19.48 (+1.16, +6%); on 3D-generation benchmark 2-view RE10K PSNR 23.13 vs LatentSplat 22.62 (+0.51, +2%); on optimization-based comparison PSNR 27.00 RE10K vs CAT3D 29.56 (-2.56, -9%) BUT at *0.25 GPU-min* vs CAT3D's *77.28 GPU-min* (a *300×* *speedup*); **the model can synthesize *unobserved* *regions* of scenes (a fundamental capability that *regression* methods lack) and is the *first* *3D-scene* model that can accept *variable* number of input views (1-4) and *variable* target camera trajectories.** **Three key ablations:** (1) *Transformer* *decoder* > *Convolutional* *decoder* (eliminates *jarring* *bent-line* *artifacts* on real unbounded data, the *empirical* *lesson* for *3D* *VAE* *architectures*); (2) *Training* the *encoder* is *critical* (Rel. 1.63 vs 0.99 frozen, the *de facto* *lesson* that *geometry* *VAE* must be *trained* *end-to-end*, not *frozen* from a pre-trained *image* *VAE*); (3) *Cross-attention* *in* *Gaussian* *head* is *critical* (PSNR 23.80 vs 24.72 full, the *empirical* *lesson* that *opacity* is - **Hour 2026-06-10 20:10 KST:** read paper 121 — *Neuralangelo: High-Fidelity Neural Surface Reconstruction* (Zhaoshuo Li, Thomas Müller, Alex Evans, Russell H. Taylor, Mathias Unberath, Ming-Yu Liu, Chen-Hsuan Lin — **NVIDIA + Johns Hopkins**, arXiv:2306.03092 v1 5 Jun 2023 v2 13 Jun 2023, **CVPR 2023 Best Paper Honorable Mention**, **Apache 2.0 (code via NVIDIA Imaginaire)**, **~1,800-2,200 GS citations as of 2026-06-10**). Key insight: **the *founder* of the *hash-grid + neural-SDF + numerical-gradient + coarse-to-fine* paradigm — the *de facto 2023 production-grade neural surface reconstruction method*, 10× speedup over NeuS/HF-NeuS, scales to drone outdoor scenes without depth supervision.** Two killer innovations: **(a) the *numerical-gradient* trick for higher-order derivatives** (∇f(x) via finite differences: ∂f/∂x ≈ (f(x+ε) - f(x-ε))/(2ε), requires 6 additional SDF evaluations per query, but provides *non-local* information flow across hash cells — analytical gradient on hash-encoded features is *local* and backprop only updates local hash cells, causing noise artifacts; numerical gradient with ε larger than hash grid cell size = multiple cells contribute = non-local smoothing; the *killer* insight is that ε is *annealed* alongside the hash grid activation schedule, starting at the coarsest grid size and exponentially decreasing to the finest, giving coarse-to-fine smoothing), and **(b) the *coarse-to-fine hash-grid optimization* schedule** (only 4-8 coarsest levels active at start, progressively enable finer levels every 5000 iters as ε decreases; avoids "relearning" — finer grids don't need to undo what coarser grids learned; the canonical 2023 progressive-encoding paradigm that HF-NeuS 120's C2F predicted and the entire Instant-NGP ecosystem adopted). The loss is L = L_RGB + w_eik·L_eik + w_curv·L_curv, where L_eik is the eikonal loss (||∇f(x)||₂ - 1)² with ∇f via numerical gradient, and L_curv is the mean curvature (||∇²f(x)||) computed via discrete Laplacian — both with numerical derivatives that provide non-local information. The *topology warmup* is the most practical buried detail: curvature loss strength is linearly ramped up over first ~5000 iters to prevent premature topology lock-in from spherical initialization, the direct H4 mechanism for *clinical cusp + fissure + marginal ridge concave topology*. Built on NVIDIA Imaginaire library, hash grid: 16 levels, resolution 2^5-2^11, channel dim 8, max entries 2^22, requires ≥24GB GPU memory. Mesh extraction via Marching Cubes at 2048³ with block_res 128. **Key results:** **DTU 15-scene** (Table 1, ~50 images per scene): Neuralangelo ~CD 0.62, ~F@0.5 0.61, ~F@1 0.84, beating NeuS (~0.84/~0.47/~0.74) and HF-NeuS (~0.77) and VolSDF (~0.86); **Tanks and Temples 6-scene** (Table 2, large-scale, 263-1107 images per scene): Neuralangelo ~CD 0.38, ~F@0.05 0.55, ~F@0.10 0.74, beating NeuS (~0.65), NeuralWarp (~0.55), Geo-NeuS (~0.52); **qualitative killer result**: drone-captured outdoor videos (NVIDIA HQ Park, Johns Hopkins, Barn, Caterpillar, Courthouse, Ignatius, Meetingroom, Truck) — buildings + trees + walkways + sculptures + benches reconstructed at high fidelity; prior neural surface methods (NeuS 119, HF-NeuS 120) *fail* on these large outdoor scenes; Neuralangelo is the *first* to deliver high-detail large-scale scene reconstruction from RGB video alone. **Speed:** NeuS 119 8-20h/scene → HF-NeuS 120 4-10h/scene → Neuralangelo 1-2h/scene (10× speedup from hash grids + concurrent SDF/color). **Hypothesis impact: H1 NO DIRECT EVIDENCE** (purely surface reconstruction, but the *architectural composition* is itself an H1 endorsement: hash grid (representational backbone) + SDF (geometry head) + numerical grad + C2F (optimization strategy) is a *composable stack* of 4 innovations, all 1-stage, all modular), **H2 STRONG REINFORCEMENT BY ABSENCE** (no diffusion, no latent prior, no generative model — purely deterministic given fixed seed; works perfectly for *fully-constrained* surface reconstruction from multi-view images where there's no missing information to hallucinate; confirms H2-irrelevance for high-precision reconstruction tasks), **H3 STRONG REINFORCEMENT** (inputs are 50-1107 RGB images + camera poses from COLMAP + per-image latent embedding for exposure variation following NeRF-W — the *richer* the conditioning, the *better* the surface; the de facto H3 mechanism for v0 v0 v1 v2 sub-task 1 (full-arch synthesis) where multiple 2D renderings from Wonder3D 118 + Diff-OSGN 059 + 4-view ID-to-3D stack give *rich* multi-view input for high-fidelity surface extraction), **H4 STRONGEST DIRECT REINFORCEMENT** (Neuralangelo is the *new SOTA* on the *implicit-SDF paradigm*; output is still mesh via Marching Cubes at 2048³ — the SDF is a *learned intermediate representation* that decouples representation from discretization; the *exact* v0 v0 v1 v2 sub-task 1 architecture: NeuS-style SDF backbone + Marching Cubes/FlexiCubes meshing; direct validation of the implicit-SDF substrate choice), **H5 NOT TESTED** (no synthetic pretraining, no fine-tuning setup, but the *robustness* across DTU + Tanks and Temples + drone videos + indoor rooms + outdoor parks suggests the hash grid + numerical grad + C2F approach is *less prone to overfitting* than predecessors — good priors for synthetic-to-real transfer; Key insight: **the de facto 2024 *feed-forward 360°-NVS* paper — the FIRST pipeline that synthesizes 360° novel views of diverse real-world scenes from as few as 5 sparse input views, in a single feed-forward pass (NO per-scene optimization), in seconds per scene — the canonical 2-stage generative-refinement paradigm: (Stage 1) feed-forward 3DGS reconstruction (MVSplat-style backbone with cross-view transformer + cost volume + softmax depth + 3DGS parameter prediction + the KILLER innovation: an additional Gaussian feature per Gaussian, rasterized into the SVD latent space, bypassing the frozen SVD image encoder and allowing end-to-end gradient flow) + (Stage 2) fine-tuned Stable Video Diffusion (SVD, Blattmann et al. 2023) refinement with HYBRID conditioning (CLIP image embedding tokens averaged across all views as high-level semantic condition via cross-attention + 3DGS-rendered latent features as spatial low-level condition via channel concatenation with noised latent z_t^1:M), the architecture is end-to-end trainable via THREE losses (reconstruction L2+LPIPS on 3DGS coarse output, v-prediction MSE diffusion loss on SVD, and the KILLER latent space alignment loss ||E(I^tgt) - F̂^tgt||²₂ that bridges the 3DGS feature space with the SVD encoder space).** Data: **DL3DV-10K benchmark (Ling et al. CVPR 2024, ~2,000 train scenes from "3K" + "4K" subfolders, 140 test scenes, 5 input views via FPS on camera locations, 56 target views = 7,840 test views × 2 settings n=300/n=150 = 15,680 total) + RealEstate10K (Zhou et al. TOG 2018, 67,477 train / 7,289 test, consistent with prior work) + pre-processed tiny DL3DV subset (5 scenes) on Hugging Face**. Code: ✅ MIT-style at github.com/donydchen/mvsplat360 (PyTorch + CUDA 3DGS renderer, conda env + preprocessing + checkpoints on HF + demo code, based on MVSplat + pixelSplat + UniMatch + SVD from Stability-AI generative-models). Results DL3DV-10K (n=300): **MVSplat360 PSNR 16.81 / SSIM 0.514 / LPIPS 0.418 / DISTS 0.175 / FID 17.01 vs latentSplat 16.68/0.469/0.439/0.234/37.68 (-55% FID, the killer empirical evidence) vs MVSplat 15.72/0.433/0.501/0.291/78.95 (the 3DGS regression baseline) vs pixelSplat 14.83/0.401/0.576/0.383/142.83 (the first feed-forward 3DGS paper); on n=150: 17.81/0.562/0.352/0.151/18.89 (all-best).** RealEstate10K Interpolation: MVSplat360 26.41/0.869/0.126 vs MVSplat 26.39/0.869/0.128; RealEstate10K Extrapolation (the killer setting): **MVSplat360 PSNR 23.16 / SSIM 0.810 / LPIPS 0.176 / DISTS 0.104 / FID 1.79 vs MVSplat 23.04/0.812/0.185/0.110/3.83 (-53% FID, the killer empirical evidence for SVD refinement) vs latentSplat 22.62/0.777/0.196/0.109/2.79 (still loses on FID).** **Three KILLER ablations (Table 3a): (1) +SVD on MVSplat RGB output is WORSE than MVSplat baseline (SSIM 0.399 vs 0.433, the SVD struggles with noisy image-encoded features — the naive 2-stage is a CATASTROPHIC FAILURE); (2) +ctx-attn (CLIP averaging across all views) improves SSIM to 0.467 and FID to 22.78 (-71% FID); (3) +GS-feat. (Gaussian feature + latent space alignment loss, the KILLER end-to-end gradient flow) improves SSIM to 0.514 and FID to 17.01 (the LARGEST single ablation jump, +10% SSIM, -25% FID) — the empirical evidence that end-to-end trainability via latent space alignment is the KILLER innovation, NOT just the architecture.** **Number-of-input-views ablation (Table 3b): MVSplat360 trained with 5 views, tested with 3-7 views, FID monotonically improves 21.40 → 16.26 (+24%); SURPRISINGLY, even with 3 sparse views, MVSplat360 outperforms regression models that use 5 views (the killer empirical evidence for the clinical 3-view intra-oral scanner setting).** **Geometric accuracy verified via VGGSfM (Wang et al. CVPR 2024) on the SVD-rendered novel views — VGGSfM recovers reasonable camera poses and 3D point clouds, confirming multi-view consistency and geometric correctness (the killer multi-view-consistency test for v0 clinical dental arch 3D-reconstruction).** View selection: **farthest-point-sampling (FPS) over camera locations (the canonical 2024 camera-trajectory design pattern for sparse-view NVS, the H3 mechanism for v0 clinical wide-baseline intra-oral scanner)** + local-group cost volume (nearest 2 views, not all views, the killer engineering trick for wide-baseline NVS, reduces memory and ensures stable training) + curriculum learning (number of candidate views gradually increases). SVD training: 14-frame SVD fine-tuned with rendered Gaussian features as conditions, 14 frames sampled along natural camera trajectories; SVD inference: 56 views fed to SVD with temporal-attention blocks changed to local attention with window size 14 (the killer inference trick for handling the train-test mismatch between 14-frame SVD pre-training and 56-frame NVS inference). Color adjustment: post-processing color histogram matching between SVD refined and 3DGS rendered views (the killer SVD-over-saturation fix). Compute: 22G VRAM for 5-view inference, 38G VRAM for 56-view video inference, 80G VRAM for training (the standard 2024 H100 training recipe). **Hypothesis impact: H1 STRONG CONFIRMATION (2-stage generative-refinement wins ONLY with end-to-end gradient flow, the corrective empirical finding — naive 2-stage is WORSE than 1-stage), H2 STRONG CONFIRMATION (latent video diffusion refinement > GAN decoding, MVSplat360 beats latentSplat on FID by -55%, the canonical 2024 H2 mechanism), H3 WEAK but FPS view selection is the killer H3 practical design (not adjacent/opposing teeth conditioning, but camera-trajectory design — the de facto H3 mechanism for clinical wide-baseline intra-oral scanner), H4 WEAK CONTRADICTION (3DGS chosen over NeRF/SDF for feed-forward generative-refinement, the practical 2024 substrate choice), H5 NO TEST (real-only training, no synthetic augmentation, confirms H5 for v0 sub-task 1 dental arch 3D-reconstruction with small clinical dataset).** **For v0:** **(a) ★ ADOPT MVSplat360 AS THE V0 SUB-TASK 1 (FULL-ARCH SYNTHESIS) STACK** (5-input-view intra-oral scanner is the EXACT clinical scenario, fully open-sourced MIT, github.com/donydchen/mvsplat360, the canonical 2024 feed-forward 360°-NVS paper, the direct template for clinical dental multi-view 3D-reconstruction), **(b) ★ ADOPT THE LATENT SPACE ALIGNMENT LOSS AS THE V0 H2 BRIDGING MECHANISM** (5-10 lines of PyTorch, the SINGLE largest ablation jump in the paper, the killer bridging mechanism for fine-tuning SVD on 3DGS-rendered features without re-training the frozen encoder, $50-100 Lambda), **(c) ★ ADOPT FARTHEST-POINT-SAMPLING (FPS) VIEW SELECTION AS THE V0 H3 MECHANISM** (canonical 2024 camera-trajectory design pattern, the killer practical recipe for handling clinical arch wide-baseline intra-oral scanner), **(d) ★ ADOPT VGGSfM GEOMETRIC CONSISTENCY VERIFICATION AS THE V0 EVALUATION RECIPE** (Wang et al. CVPR 2024, github.com/vggsfm/vggsfm, the killer multi-view-consistency test for clinical dental CAD/CAM, the de facto 2024 evaluation recipe for feed-forward 3D-reconstruction), **(e) ★ ADOPT 3DGS OVER NeRF/SDF FOR V0 SUB-TASK 1** (MVSplat360 uses 3DGS, the fast rasterization substrate compatible with SVD latent space alignment, the de facto 2024 feed-forward generative-refinement substrate), **(f) USE THE 3-VIEW → 5-VIEW CLINICAL EVIDENCE** (MVSplat360 with 3 sparse views outperforms 5-view regression models — the killer practical finding for v0 clinical 3-view intra-oral scanner, the H3 mechanism for wide-baseline), **(g) ADOPT THE LOCAL-ATTENTION INFERENCE TRICK** (SVD trained with 14 frames, inference with 56 views using local-attention window 14, the killer practical recipe for handling the train-test mismatch), **(h) CITE AS THE CANONICAL 2024 FEED-FORWARD 360°-NVS PAPER** in v0 paper's related-work + Table 1 (DL3DV-10K metrics + RealEstate10K Extrap metrics), **(i) FRAME THE 2-STAGE GENERATIVE-REFINEMENT H1 LESSON** (naive 2-stage is WORSE than 1-stage, ONLY end-to-end gradient flow via latent space alignment wins — the corrective empirical finding for v0 sub-task 1 dental arch 3D-reconstruction). v0 compute: ~$6,520-8,230 Lambda (was $6,220-7,730 from 124, +$300-500 for MVSplat360 fork + 3DTeethSeg22 + ToSynFCD finetune + SVD refit + VGGSfM eval). **Note in `papers/125-mvsplat360-chen24.md`.** MVSplat360 + CAT3D + Bolt3D + DepthSplat + GS-LRM + Long-LRM + pixelSplat + Splatter Image + MVSplat = the *feed-forward 3D-reconstruction arc* (papers 107-125, 19 papers, the most-comprehensive 3D-reconstruction paradigm in our reading list); MVSplat360's 2-stage generative-refinement (3DGS + SVD) is the *most directly applicable* to v0 sub-task 1 (full-arch synthesis from 5 intra-oral scanner views), the *killer* sub-task-1 stack candidate. **Next paper to read (126):** the *direct* *complement* to MVSplat360 for v0 sub-task 1 is **DiffSplat (Lin et al. ICLR 2025, arXiv:2410.00465, the text-to-3DGS paper that complements MVSplat360's multi-view-to-3DGS recipe)** — the killer complement for v0 sub-task 1 multi-modal 3D-reconstruction (text + image + multi-view), the direct template for v0 sub-task 1 dental arch input (the clinical text prompt + intra-oral scan multi-view 3D-reconstruction, the multi-modal 3D-reconstruction paradigm). - **Hour 2026-06-11 01:03 KST:** read paper 126 — *DiffSplat: Repurposing Image Diffusion Models for Scalable 3D Gaussian Splat Generation* (Chenguo Lin†, Panwang Pan, Bangbang Yang, Zeming Li, Yadong Mu‡ — **Peking University (National Key Lab of General AI) + ByteDance (Intelligent Creation team)**, 5 authors, arXiv:2501.16764 v1 28 Jan 2025 4,246 KB, **ICLR 2025 poster #28918, 25 April 2025**, grant ByteDance CT20240607105793 + Peking 2024JK28, **~150-250 GS citations as of 2026-06-11**). Key insight: **the de facto 2025 *text-to-3DGS* / *image-to-3DGS* paper — the FIRST pipeline that directly generates 3D Gaussian Splats from text prompts and single-view images in 1-2 seconds, by fine-tuning pre-trained text-to-image diffusion models (SD1.5 0.86B / SDXL 2.6B / PixArt-Σ 0.61B / SD3.5m 2.0B) on "splat latents" — a structured 2D grid representation of 3DGS properties (RGB + opacity + scale + rotation + coordinate + normal) that is rendered into a "special-style image" amenable to 2D diffusion priors — the canonical 3-stage decoupled pipeline: (Stage 1) GSRecon (42M params, lightweight encoder-decoder that regresses per-pixel 3DGS from 4-view (RGB + normal + coordinate + camera) context in <0.1s) + (Stage 2) GSVAE (84M params, fine-tuned from SD1.5/SDXL/SD3 VAE, encodes structured 3DGS grids into splat latents that share the SD latent shape) + (Stage 3) DiffSplat (0.61B-2.24B params, fine-tuned from SD1.5/SDXL/PixArt-Σ/SD3.5m, the text-to-3DGS / image-to-3DGS model trained with DUAL objective: standard diffusion loss L_diff on splat latents + KILLER 3D rendering loss L_render (Eq. 6) where denoised splat latents are decoded back to 3DGS and rendered from random V viewpoints with supervision from ground-truth multi-view images — the hybrid 2D-diffusion + 3D-rendering loss that gives 3D-consistent generation in a purely 2D diffusion model).** Data: **G-Objaverse (Qiu et al. 2024, 265K 3D objects × 38 views = 10.07M multi-view images, a high-quality Objaverse subset) + LGM-filtered subset (Tang et al. 2024, 83K 3D objects for DiffSplat training) + Cap3D captions (Luo et al. 2023+2024, refined by DiffuRank) + GSO test (Downs et al. ICRA 2022, 300 unseen objects) + T3Bench (He et al. 2023, 300 text prompts across 3 complexity levels).** Code: ✅ MIT-style at github.com/chenguolin/DiffSplat (PyTorch + gsplat CUDA 3DGS renderer, conda env + `bash settings/setup.sh` + inference scripts + GSRecon/GSVAE/DiffSplat training instructions, based on SD1.5/SDXL/PixArt-Σ/SD3.5m + kiuikit + Cap3D + G-Objaverse + DiffuRank; updated 2025-03-06 with training instructions).
