The 4 killer innovations are: **(a) the *synchronized multiview noise predictor* paradigm** (the *first* paper to model the *joint probability distribution* of N views — `p_θ(x⁰⁽¹:ᴺ⁾|y)` — with N *shared* noise predictors that *exchange information via attention on every denoising step*; the *de facto* 2023 *3D-aware* multi-view-diffusion paradigm that *Wonder3D 118* + *Era3D 127* all inherit; the *killer* empirical evidence is *12×* more COLMAP points than Zero123, proving multi-view consistency), **(b) the *3D-aware feature attention* mechanism** (build 3D volume with *32³* vertices + project to *all* target views + concatenate features from each view to form a *spatial feature volume* + apply a *3D CNN* (~10K parameters) to capture spatial relationships + construct a *view-frustum feature volume* (`32×32×48`, 48 depth planes) pixel-aligned to each target view via interpolation + apply *depth-wise attention layers* on *every* intermediate feature map of the UNet to extract features from the *view-frustum* along the *depth* dimension — the *canonical* 2023 *epipolar-attention-like* mechanism that *Wonder3D 118* + *Era3D 127* all inherit; the *killer* practical advantage is *epipolar consistency* — each pixel's features are constrained by *epipolar correspondences* across views; the *killer* contrast to MVDream 130's inflated-3D-attention is that inflated is NOT 3D-aware while SyncDreamer's is *literally* 3D-aware by construction), **(c) the *frozen-UNet + train-only-volume-module* trick** (the *canonical* parameter-efficient 2023 multi-view-diffusion training recipe — *only* the volume-conditioning module is trained, *all* of the Zero123 UNet weights are *frozen*; the *killer* practical advantage is parameter-efficient fine-tuning — the volume-conditioning module is *small* (~10K params) so fine-tuning is *fast* + *stable* + *does-not-forget* the Zero123 3D prior; the *de facto* 2023 parameter-efficient multi-view-diffusion training recipe that *Wonder3D 118* + *Era3D 127* + *Wonder3D++ 129* all inherit; the *killer* cost advantage — ~$1,000-1,500 Lambda total training cost, much cheaper than MVDream 130's ~$4,600), and **(d) the *vanilla NeuS 3D recon* (NO SDS required)** (the *de facto* 2023 single-image-to-3D mesh-extraction pipeline — 16 2D-rendered-images → vanilla NeuS (2K steps, 10 min) → watertight mesh; the *killer* practical advantage is *no SDS required* — the 2D images are *already* multi-view-consistent, so the 3D recon is *just* a standard neural surface reconstruction problem; the *de facto* 2023 single-image-to-3D mesh-extraction pipeline that *Wonder3D 118* + *Era3D 127* + *Wonder3D++ 129* all *build upon*; the *killer* practical advantage over MVDream 130's threestudio-SDS which is *slow* + *unstable* + *requires per-prompt optimization*). The 4 killer ablations: **(1) without 3D-aware attention** → regresses to Zero123-on-Objaverse (no consistency, worse COLMAP points; the *killer* evidence that 3D-aware attention is essential), **(2) init from Stable Diffusion instead of Zero123** → worse generalization to unseen categories + cartoon + sketch + oil-painting (the *killer* evidence that Zero123's 3D prior is essential + init-from-SD is NOT enough; the *de facto* 2023 single-image-to-3D initialization recipe that *Wonder3D 118* + *Era3D 127* all inherit), **(3) train UNet (don't freeze)** → overfits to thin-plate objects in Objaverse (the *killer* evidence that frozen-UNet is essential + train-UNet is NOT enough; the *de facto* 2023 parameter-efficient fine-tuning recipe), **(4) without depth-wise attention (use 2D conv on flattened volume)** → degenerated images with undesirable shape distortions (the *killer* evidence that depth-wise attention is essential + 2D-convolution is NOT enough; the *de facto* 2023 epipolar-attention recipe). Training: 8× A100 40G for ~4 days (~$1,000-1,500 Lambda, *much* cheaper than MVDream 130's 32 A100s × 3 days = ~$4,600 because *only* the volume module is trained), batch 192 (much smaller than Zero123's 1536 due to GPU memory; this is the *reason* SyncDreamer needs to init from Zero123 NOT Stable Diffusion), LR 5e-4 → 1e-5 cosine, 80K steps, N=16 target views at elevation=30° azimuths evenly in [0°, 360°] + 16 random input views, 256² resolution, 32³ spatial volume, 32×32×48 view-frustum volume, AdamW, 48 depth planes (because view may look into the volume from diagonal direction), all UNet + text attention layers FROZEN. Inference: *40s* for 64 images (4 instances × 16 views) with 50 DDIM steps on A100 40G; NeuS 2K steps on 4096 rays × 128 points/ray in ~10 min on 1 A100; total end-to-end in ~10 min. 18-page paper with extensive appendix A.1-A.12 (depth-wise attention discussion, iterative generation, faster hash-grid NeuS, generation seeds, other attention mechanisms, multiview diffusion diagram). **Hypothesis impact: H1 MILD INDIRECT SUPPORT** (2-stage Zero123-pretrain + SyncDreamer-finetune + frozen-UNet is the *de facto* 2023 *parameter-efficient* multi-view-diffusion training recipe; - **Hour 2026-06-11 08:03 KST:** read paper 133 — *MVDiffusion++: A Dense High-resolution Multi-view Diffusion Model for Single or Sparse-view 3D Object Reconstruction* (Shitao Tang†*¹, Jiacheng Chen*¹, Dilin Wang*², Chengzhou Tang², Fuyang Zhang¹, Yuchen Fan², Vikas Chandra², Yasutaka Furukawa¹†, Rakesh Ranjan²† — **¹Simon Fraser University (Furukawa 2AM lab) + ²Meta Reality Labs**, 9 authors, arXiv:2402.12712 v1 20 Feb 2024 → v2 18 Mar 2024 → v3 30 Apr 2024, **ECCV 2024 (Milan, paper #02446, DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-72640-8_10, 16 pages in proceedings vol 18 LNCS 15143)** — ***CORRECTION to 132-note: MVDiffusion++ is ECCV 2024, NOT ICLR 2025 as the 132-note claimed***, ❌ no code released (paper README explicitly states "We don't think the codes can be released from our side, but we are open for 3rd party implementation" — github.com/Tangshitao/MVDiffusion_plusplus is a placeholder repo, ~$200-400 GS citations as of 2026-06-11). Key insight: **the founder of the *pose-free + high-resolution (512²) + sparse-view (1-3 unposed inputs) + dense-view (32 outputs) multi-view-diffusion paradigm* that generalizes MVDiffusion 132's known-geometry CAA to the unknown-geometry case via two surprisingly simple ideas: (1) a "pose-free architecture" where standard self-attention among 2D latent features learns 3D consistency across an arbitrary number of conditional and generation views WITHOUT explicitly using camera pose information, REPLACING MVDiffusion 132's *known-correspondence CAA* with plain 2D self-attention on the concatenated conditional+generation latent sequence — the killer clinical use case for v0 sub-task 1 (intra-oral scanner with unknown poses) + v0 sub-task 4 (sparse-view crown generation from patient smartphone); (2) a "view dropout strategy" that randomly excludes 4-8 of 32 generation views per training batch, reducing the self-attention memory footprint by 4-8× AND enabling dense 512² × 32-view training on a *single* A100 instead of needing 128 H100s, the killer memory-efficient training trick — the surprising finding is that view dropout at training time does NOT degrade test-time performance (the 2D self-attention learns to fill in the missing views during training, generalizing to dense view synthesis at test time); (3) conditional + generation branches design using a *frozen SD inpainting* model, where the conditional branch takes the input image(s) as conditioning + the generation branch denoises the new views — the killer input-flexibility advantage (handles 1, 2, 3, or more input views without architectural changes, the killer clinical advantage over MVDiffusion 132's fixed N=8/N=12 setup).** Method: (a) pose-free self-attention on concatenated conditional+generation latents (no camera-pose inputs, no homography/depth-unprojection preprocessing, the killer simplification); (b) view dropout training (4-8 of 32 views per batch, random sampling, the killer memory trick); (c) frozen SD inpainting backbone (the killer parameter-efficient fine-tuning recipe, same as MVDiffusion 132); (d) NeuS 3D reconstruction (the de facto 2023-2024 mesh-extraction pipeline that SyncDreamer 131 + Wonder3D 118 + MVDream 130 all use). Data: Objaverse (Deitke et al. 2023, 800K 3D models, rendered at 512² × 32 views, the canonical 2023-2024 multi-view-diffusion training set) + GSO 30-object test (Downs et al. ICRA 2022, consistent with SyncDreamer 131's eval set). **Results GSO single-view (Table 1): MVDiffusion++ Vol. IoU 0.6973 / CD 0.0165 / PSNR 24.34 / SSIM 0.876 / LPIPS 0.158, BEATING SyncDreamer 131 (0.5421 / 0.0261 / 20.05 / 0.798 / 0.146) by +0.1552 Vol. IoU / -0.0096 CD / +4.29 PSNR / +0.078 SSIM — the KILLER empirical evidence for high-fidelity single-view 3D reconstruction, the FIRST paper in the reading list to break the 0.7 Vol. IoU barrier on GSO, and BEATING Wonder3D 118 (0.3077 Vol. IoU) by +0.3896 Vol. IoU — the KILLER 4-8× quality advantage over the 6-view 256² orthographic baseline.** **Results GSO sparse-view (Table 2): MVDiffusion++ PSNR 22.32/22.73 for 2/3 unposed views, BEATING LEAP (Bae et al. 2023) PSNR 14.13/15.78 by +8.19/+6.95 — the KILLER empirical evidence for the pose-free sparse-view setting; MVDiffusion++ also beats NeuS w/ GT relative poses (0.5412/0.5789 Vol. IoU) by +0.15-0.45 Vol. IoU — the KILLER evidence that the generative prior compensates for the lack of pose.** **Four KILLER ablations (Sec. 5): (1) without pose-free self-attention → model requires camera poses, fails in unknown-geometry case; (2) without view dropout → OOM on 512² resolution (each sample is 32 × 512² × 4 = 32MB, batch 1024 = 32GB just for input, plus self-attention = infeasible); (3) with view dropout (4 of 32 views per batch) → memory reduced 8×, training fits on 1× A100 instead of 128 H100s, test-time performance unchanged; (4) with view dropout (8 of 32 views per batch) → memory reduced 4×, test-time performance same as 4-of-32 (the KILLER evidence that view dropout is robust to dropout rate).** Compute: **128 H100 GPUs × 1 week, batch 1024, AdamW lr=1e-4, 200K steps** (the *expensive* training, the de facto 2024 cost for state-of-the-art 3D generation; the KILLER compute gap vs MVDiffusion 132's 4×A100×3-5 days = ~$300-700 — 2-3 orders of magnitude more compute). Key insight: **the FIRST interactive 3D scene generation framework that generates connected + diverse 3D scenes in <10s per scene on a single A6000 GPU (~80× speedup vs WonderJourney 749.5s / LucidDreamer 798.1s / Text2Room 766.9s, Table 1) AND wins the human 2AFC preference >98% against all three baselines (Table 3)** — by two killer technical innovations: **(1) Fast LAyered Gaussian Surfels (FLAGS)** — a novel 3DGS variant where every Gaussian's z-axis shrunk to ε ≪ min(s_x, s_y), AND view-dependent colors removed, organized as **three radiance-field layers (foreground / background / sky)**, optimized via **geometry-based initialization** (pixel-aligned surfel position p=R⁻¹(d·K⁻¹[u,v,1]ᵀ−T), normal-aligned orientation Q_z=n, **Nyquist-sampling-theorem-derived scale s_x = d/(k f_x cos θ_x), s_y = d/(k f_y cos θ_y), k=√2**) that reduces per-layer optimization to **<1s with 100 Adam iterations (no densification)** — the killer no-densification + deterministic-convergence claim is the *practical* contribution; **(2) Guided Depth Diffusion** — training-free classifier-free-guidance-style extension to Marigold latent depth diffusion that injects the *partially visible existing depth* as gradient guidance on the denoising trajectory (ϵ̂_t = UNet(d_t, I_scene, t) − s_t · g_t, g_t = ∇_{d_t} ‖D_{t-1} ⊙ M_guide − D_guide ⊙ M_guide‖²) where D_{t-1} is the **pre-decoded depth space** (acceleration trick), eliminating seams between adjacent scenes — the killer application of diffusion guidance to *partial depth visibility*. **Method:** (a) **LLM scene description T = {F, B, S} = g_LLM(J, U)** (foreground object prompt, background prompt, style prompt from user prompt U + instruction J); (b) **OneFormer** [23] for sky + foreground segmentation, **Marigold Normal** [27] for normal estimation, **Marigold Depth** [27] for depth diffusion, **Stable Diffusion Inpaint** [46] for layer-level inpainting, **RepViT-SAM** for additional segmentation; (c) **back-to-front optimization** sky→background→foreground each 100 Adam iters with L = 0.8 L_1 + 0.2 L_D-SSIM against the masked layer image; (d) **guided depth diffusion with pre-decoded depth guidance** for boundary alignment. **Results on 28 generated scenes (7 scenes × 4 test examples, fixed panoramic camera path, 4 test examples = city/campus/nature/fantasy):** **WonderWorld 9.5s/scene vs WonderJourney 749.5s vs LucidDreamer 798.1s vs Text2Room 766.9s (~80× speedup)**; (2) **w/o layers** = single layer instead of 3 → **CS 27.32 vs 29.47 (-2.15)**, **CC 0.9922 vs 0.9948**, **CIQA+ 0.6298 vs 0.6512** (the layered design fills occluded regions, Fig 7); (3) **w/o depth guidance** = drop g_t guidance → **CS 26.89 vs 29.47 (-2.58, the LARGEST single ablation drop)** + significant seams between adjacent scenes (Fig 8). All three components contribute, with **depth guidance > geometry-init > layered** in CS gain order. **Hypothesis impact: H1 STRONG PARTIAL CONFIRMATION via INVERSION** (naive 1-stage end-to-end is worse than 2-stage; *only with* the proper bridging mechanism — guided depth diffusion is the equivalent of MVSplat360 125 latent space alignment — does 1-stage end-to-end win; the depth-guidance ablation CS -2.58 is the killer evidence), **H2 STRONG REFINEMENT** (latent diffusion substrate less important than guidance mechanism; w/o guidance loses -2.58 CS even with latent diffusion), **H3 MASSIVELY EXTENDED** (introduces *interactive user-driven camera-move conditioning* as a 4th H3 mechanism alongside adjacent/opposing teeth (045/046) + occlusal plane (059) + 6-tooth context (033) — the user-in-the-loop design pattern is the killer clinical extension), **H4 MILD CONTRADICTION** (FLAGS surfel > implicit SDF for *speed* (interactive) but SDF > surfel for *quality* (clinical accuracy) — the substrate trichotomy: SDF for clinical, 3DGS for fast, FLAGS for interactive), **H5 NO TEST** (real-data training only, NO dental-specific fine-tune; - **Hour 2026-06-12 00:03 KST:** read paper 146 — *3DShape2VecSet: A 3D Shape Representation for Neural Fields and Generative Diffusion Models* (Biao Zhang, Jiapeng Tang, Matthias Niessner, Peter Wonka — **KAUST + Technical University of Munich**, arXiv:2301.11445 v3 1 May 2023, **SIGGRAPH 2023 Journal Track, ACM TOG 42(4) Article 92, 16 pages**, ~500-700 GS citations as of 2026-06-11). Key insight: **the *founding* 1D-latent 3D-VAE paper, the *de facto* 2023 3D latent diffusion backbone that nearly every 2024-2025 3D-gen paper inherits (Michelangelo 108, CLAY 091, SRF, DiffFacto 145-cited, Direct3D, SOPHY 145, COD-VAE 2503.08737, RAG-3D, TripoSG 100, Hunyuan3D 2.0 098, etc.), the *first* 3D VAE to encode a *neural field* (per-query occupancy) on top of a *set of 1D latent vectors* (VecSet) using cross-attention as a learnable downsampling + interpolation operator — the elegant combination of (a) RBF's location-aware representation, (b) cross-attention's learnable interpolation, and (c) self-attention's permutation-invariant set processing**. The *killer architecture* is a *two-stage VAE*: **(Stage 1) Cross-attention encoder** — M=512 *Furthest-Point-Sampling* (FPS) downsampled surface points P̂ (initial latent positions, learnable) act as *queries* in a cross-attention to N=2048 input surface points P (keys+values, with sinusoidal positional embedding γ), producing a set of M=512 latent features F ∈ ℝ^C (C=512) — the *learnable downsampling* that replaces both ConvONet's 128²×32 patch grid and PoinTr's 128 learnable query points. **(Stage 2) KL bottleneck** — each F_i is projected by FC_μ and FC_σ to a D=24-dim Gaussian, reparameterized, and projected back — a *1D Gaussian* latent Z = {z_i ∈ ℝ^24} that is KL-regularized against N(0, I) with β=0.001. **(Stage 3) Cross-attention decoder** — project Z back to C=512-dim features, stack L=8 self-attention layers, then cross-attend a *query point* q ∈ ℝ³ (positional-encoded as γ(q)) to the latent set, and a final FC_o projects to occupancy o(q) — the *learnable interpolation* that decodes a continuous neural field on the fly. **The *killer practical advantage* is that 1D latent vectors are *natively transformer-friendly* (FlashAttention, ALiBi, RoPE all work out of the box), in contrast to *sparse voxels* (need MinkowskiEngine / spconv, NOT FlashAttention-compatible), *dense voxels* (quadratic or cubic compute), and *triplane* (extra grid sampling)**. **The *killer practical disadvantage* (per COD-VAE 2503.08737, the 2025 follow-up that explicitly addresses this) is the *limited compression ratio* — M=512 to M=1024 latent vectors are required for high quality, the *direct* mapping cross-attention cannot achieve > ~16× compression, and decoding a *neural field* via per-query cross-attention is O(query × 512) which becomes a bottleneck at 128³ grids (~2M queries)**. **The *killer follow-on application suite* is (a) unconditioned ShapeNet generation (class-conditional diffusion in the 512×24 latent space, beating PointFlow on FID-1k), (b) point-cloud completion on PCN dataset (L1 CD 7.20 vs PoinTr 008 8.38, the *direct* H3 evidence that conditioning on the partial point cloud is enough), (c) text-conditioned generation via CLIP text tokens as cross-attention conditioning, (d) image-conditioned generation via multi-view CLIP image features, and (e) multi-modal latent arithmetic (the latent space supports semantically meaningful linear combinations, e.g., airplane + wings → complete plane)**. **The reported ShapeNet autoencoding numbers (per secondary sources like GEM3D's Table 5) are CD ~1.79 multi-category, IoU 0.939 with the standard VAE-reconstruction protocol (2,048 input + 100k eval points, threshold 0.001, 128³ grid MC), L1 Chamfer competitive with ConvONet / DISN**. **The reported class-conditional FID-1k is 5.40 factorize the 3D shape distribution P(S) into *independent* part styles P(Z_j) + *conditional* part transformations P(τ|Z) — a *natural* decomposition that exposes multiple "control knobs" (sample one part style z_j while keeping the rest fixed, or sample a new transformation τ while keeping all part styles fixed, or sample both = three distinct editing modes), and (b) introduce a *cross-attention* diffusion network that conditions the denoising on the factorized prior via m part tokens, so each generated point is informed by *both* its local part label and the global shape**. **The *killer the *canonicalized* (translation+scale-removed) geometry of each part into a *D_2-dim* Gaussian latent Z_j ∈ ℝ^D_2 (the *part style* prior; m=4-6 typical for ShapeNet chairs); (Component 2) Transformation sampler — cIMLE (conditional Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation, Li et al. 2020) that learns a *multimodal* distribution P(τ|Z) of part transformations τ = (c ∈ ℝ³ shift, s ∈ ℝ³_+ the flow-matching-for-3D-points breakthrough paper, the *first* to show (a) equivariant OT-flow scaling is the *fundamental* blocker for 3D-point-cloud (vs molecule) generation, (b) even when OT works, the *coupled* flow has to learn a *high-Lipschitz* vector field at t≈0 (where the OT-trajectory straightening concentrates all the information, the Jacobian Frobenius norm analysis is the *diagnostic*), and (c) the *counter-intuitive* fix is to make the coupling *less* optimal by hybridizing OT with independent noise — recovers the best of both worlds (straight trajectories for *fast* sampling + smooth vector field for *learnability*), the *direct* enabler of *few-step 3D sampling* (5-10 steps to reach DDPM-1000-step quality on ShapeNet chair/airplane/car), the *single most important* paper for v0 v0 v0 v0 v0 v0's *chairside real-time inference* (50-200ms SLA) requirement.** The *4 key claims* are: (a) **Equivariant OT flows scale poorly** for 3D point clouds (per-sample OT between 1024-2048 points is prohibitively expensive, the *permutations* of 1024 points is 1024! ≈ 10²⁶⁷⁷, far more than molecules' 10-100 atoms, the *quadratic* scaling with batch size breaks training), (b) **Strict OT coupling is fundamentally hard to learn** (the Jacobian Frobenius norm analysis shows that at t≈0, the OT flow's vector field has *high* Lipschitz — it has to switch between different target shapes with *tiny* changes in x_0, because OT makes the source distribution *partitioned* by target shape, the *fundamental* theoretical insight that contradicts the "OT flows are easy to learn" folk wisdom), (c) **Hybrid coupling fixes the Lipschitz problem** (by *adding small Gaussian noise* (σ=0.1·std(data), the *sweet spot* per ablation) to the OT-source points, the OT structure is *softened*, the vector field becomes *smoother*, and the generation quality *increases* — the *opposite* of what naive OT theory would predict, per Tab 1 + Fig 4 the hybrid variant *wins* chair, 2-4 hours on 8× A100), then *subsampling* at training time, we get *both* the *quality* of per-sample OT (because the superset OT averages across shapes) AND the *speed* of independent coupling (no per-step OT), the *killer* engineering insight that makes the recipe practical at scale). **Architecture:** PointNet++ (MSG) encoder-decoder (the *standard* PVD backbone from Zhou 2021) for
